text:
☀️The unique Durga Puja where Maa Durga never departs and there is no immersion of the Devi Murti☀️

✨The Bagbazar Halder Bari Durga Puja in North Kolkata is one of the city's oldest and most fascinating Bonedi Bari (aristocratic household) pujas. Celebrating over 450 years of uninterrupted tradition, this family puja stands out from Kolkata's usual theme-based pandals because it revolves around a permanent, centuries-old touchstone idol and entirely unconventional rituals.

1. The Core Secret: A Mystical Vision & The Deeply Buried Idol.
Unlike traditional Durga Pujas where a clay idol is crafted and immersed in the river every year, Halder Bari worships a permanent, 2+ feet tall Mahisasuramardini idol carved from a single slab of Kosthipathor (touchstone).
According to family history, the ancestors originally lived in Chandannagar. During a trip to Baleshwar (Odisha), a family member had a vivid dream where Goddess Durga commanded them to excavate Her stone idol. Following the precise instructions from the vision, the family dug 14 feet beneath a fisherman's hut and unearthed this pristine touchstone Idol. Historians believe the idol dates back to the ancient Pal Dynasty. Devotees likely buried it deep underground centuries earlier to shield it from destruction during foreign invasions.

2. The Unique Rituals That Break Common Traditions
The Halder family observes several distinct rituals that set them apart from mainstream Durga Puja conventions:
No Immersion (Bisarjan): Because the idol is made of solid stone, there is no immersion on Dashami. Instead, the family updates the spiritual energy by changing the sacred Ghat (pot) water. The idol is painted only once every 12 years.
The Changing Directions: For 355 days a year, the idol faces West inside the home. However, from Mahalaya to Dashami, she is turned to face South to oversee the special Durga Puja rituals.
Maa Durga Stands Alone: You will not find forms of Lakshmi, Saraswati, Kartik, or Ganesh here. Maa Durga is worshipped as a solo warrior Goddess, flanked only by Her companion deities, Jaya, Vijaya, and Mahakal.
Strict Leather Ban: Because the Deity is permanently residing in the house, the inner sanctum is treated with severe purity. Visitors and family members are strictly forbidden from wearing leather items like belts, wallets, bags, or leather watch straps near the altar.

3. On Shashthi, the Goddess is offered Ghi Bhaat (clarified butter rice) with five types of fries, including mandatory winter melon and butter beans, followed by Payesh (rice pudding).
The Sacred Weight Rule: Every single day, the ingredients used to cook the Goddess's food offerings (rice, lentils, and milk for sweets) must weigh exactly Five Po (an ancient measurement roughly equal to 1.25 kg). This precise weight has been followed strictly for over four centuries.

4. Special Spectacles During the Puja Days
The Procession of Giant Umbrellas: On Saptami morning, during the Nabapatrika Snan (the bathing of the banana bride plant), the two branches of the Halder family march to the Ganga river at the Bagbazar Sarada Mayer Ghat together. They shield the sacred plants under two massive, intricately embroidered heirloom umbrellas, creating an incredible visual spectacle through the streets of North Kolkata.
The Eternal Flame (Jaag Pradip): On Shashthi, a specialized large oil lamp called the Jaag Pradip is lit. It is guarded relentlessly by family members to ensure it burns continuously without going out for all five days of the festival.

✨🪷Jai Maa Durga, Jai Maa Durga, Jai Maa Durga 🪷✨

$VICR  is definitely one of the most volatile stocks I hold. Here’s my take after the earnings report:

1. Q3 Financials (Double Beat):
• Revenue: $197.1M (+37.5% QoQ, +78.5% YoY) vs. $172M consensus.
• Gross Margin: 68.3% (up from 58% in Q2).
• Net Income: $63.3M, GAAP diluted EPS of $1.33 vs. $1.18 consensus.
• Royalty revenue: +119% QoQ to $66.6M.

2. Licensing Moat & ITC Leverage: Royalties are now recurring. The Q4 baseline is pegged at a conservative $43M with no new deals signed. The first pure VPD license was inked with a lead AI OEM, with more pipeline incoming. 

Vicor’s royalty framework is lethal: if an infringer doesn't settle at Stage 0 and forces ITC litigation (as seen with Foxconn and others), royalty rates escalate by ~5% every single month until trial. The ultimate threat? A complete US import ban on infringing AI servers.

3. The Engineering Moat: AI processors are crossing 1,000–1,500A+ limits, where PCB copper simply melts under lateral distribution losses. Vicor’s Vertical Power Delivery (VPD) places modules directly beneath the silicon to step down 48V to <1V. 

Current hardware is at 1.5mm thickness; they hit 1.0mm in 6 months. 
Competitors are still stuck above 3mm. 
Bonus diversification: their ATE (semiconductor test equipment) segment is already generating $100M+/yr in steady, high-margin revenue.

4. 5x Capacity Expansion (Zero Debt):Secured sites for Fab-2 and Fab-3 (5x+ footprint upside). 
Fab-2 (330k sq ft existing facility) gets its first equipment in Q2 2027. 
With $513M in cash and zero debt, the entire capex buildout is funded via operating cash flow.

5. Napkin Math:
 Q3 EPS of $1.33 = ~$5.32 run-rate. 
At a ~38x P/E, shares trade at ~$200 (including ~$11/share in net cash). 

• Long-Term Target: Management aims for $2.5B revenue at 40% operating margin, translating to ~$800M net income and ~$16.80 EPS. 

Even if the multiple compresses to 20x P/E, you get ~$335/share; at 25x, it’s ~$420.

 A volatile name, but dips into the $180–$190 zone offer an attractive entry ahead of the Fab-2 ramp in 2027.

2027 NFL Draft: Talent at Every Turn

A generational receiver, intriguing quarterbacks, and three top-13 picks give the Jets a rare opportunity to reshape their future.

After completing Version 3.0 of my 2027 first-round projection, my biggest takeaway is the variety of ways teams can improve. From explosive playmakers to disruptive defenders and versatile offensive linemen, this class offers building blocks throughout the opening round.

Jeremiah Smith leads my board. I view the Ohio State receiver as a generational prospect whose size, explosiveness, body control, and exceptional ball skills could transform an offense. My projection sends Smith first overall to the Los Angeles Chargers, giving their passing game a potential centerpiece.

The quarterback picture looks different in this version. With Arch Manning, Dante Moore, and Drew Mestemaker projected to remain in college, Darian Mensah goes second to Miami. CJ Carr lands sixth with the Jets, Trinidad Chambliss seventh with Philadelphia, and Jayden Maiava closes the round with Minnesota.

No team has a more compelling opportunity than New York. With selections at Nos. 6, 10, and 13, the Jets can address three foundational needs. My projection pairs Carr with disruptive Ole Miss defensive tackle Will Echoles and versatile Minnesota interior lineman Greg Johnson. That combination strengthens the quarterback position and both lines.

Cleveland also holds two first-round selections, adding Georgia corner Ellis Robinson IV and Indiana tackle Carter Smith.

What stands out most is the depth beyond the headliners. Premium positions remain represented throughout the round, giving teams multiple paths toward improvement. For the Jets, especially, this draft could establish the foundation for a lasting turnaround.

text:
SPARE US, HARRY!! You want peace with your father and your brother, so naturally you went to GQ?!?!

Asked whether he grieves his relationships with the King and William, the Duke of Sussex replied: "Some people don't want it to work out. I want it to work out." Reconciling, he said, is "the most important thing".

Some people. He was asked about exactly two people.

Within hours his spokesman was insisting it was no swipe at his brother or anyone else in the family. THEN WHO, PRAY?!? The question named two men, and he answered it.

And the olive branch came with conditions attached. "I can respect them if they respect me and our position," Harry said. "Our position is really quite clear now." Respect on his terms, offered to the Sovereign through an American glossy.

Think about how this "reconciliation" is actually being run. A memoir. A plea for peace in a television interview in May 2025. Now another, on camera, in New York. In the very same sitting he explained why he keeps talking: he would rather put things out himself than leave it to "the machine", and he complained that he has been "really criticized for telling my story”.

Oh and we are still waiting for such a reconciliation among the Markles, except they cannot provide the coaches and castles.

So the man who says healing the rift matters more than anything has a standing policy of narrating it. Every private word his father or brother offers now carries an obvious question. Will it turn up in the next interview?

Trust is not something you can ask for through a lens. Each new camera he sits in front of shuts the door he claims to want open.

Even his interviewer seemed unmoved. When Harry explained he wanted no sympathy "because I'm a prince", the reply came back: "So?"

His camp says the interview was recorded in late September, that GQ alone chose the release date, and that nothing should be read into the timing. Yes, still, it landed on the very day his family welcomed the Sultan of Oman.

Look at what that family did with the day.

A carriage procession through Windsor. A Guard of Honour. That evening, a state banquet for 160 in St George's Hall, where the King praised Oman's efforts to keep the Strait of Hormuz open while war rages with Iran. He singled out William's work alongside the Sultan's son. Catherine, radiant, was there for the welcome and the banquet.

Harry did not rate a mention in the speech. He is not a working royal.

This morning the King, Queen and Prince of Wales were in Aberfan, sixty years to the day since a colliery tip buried Pantglas Junior School and killed 116 children and 28 adults. The King and William laid wreaths. The Queen placed a posy. Then they went on to meet survivors and bereaved families.

That is duty and dignity. Compare it to the Sussex circus.

His father and brother spent this week working. Harry's contribution was a chat for his own benefit with GQ.

text:
October 21 — John Bunyan: Twelve Years in Prison for Preaching the Gospel

Martyrdom, Steadfastness & Sacrifice

Historical Context

Yesterday, we examined Mary Dyer, the Quaker woman executed in colonial Massachusetts for defying laws against religious dissent. Today we return to England, where another Christian endured years of imprisonment rather than surrender his calling to preach.

His name was John Bunyan (1628–1688), and his imprisonment would eventually help produce one of the most influential works of Christian literature ever written: The Pilgrim's Progress.

Bunyan was born near Bedford, England, into a modest family. His father worked as a tinker, repairing pots and metal household goods, and Bunyan followed the same trade. He received a limited formal education but developed a remarkable familiarity with Scripture.

As a young man, Bunyan experienced intense religious anxiety concerning sin, salvation, and the condition of his soul. He eventually joined a congregation of Christians who worshipped independently of the established Church of England.

During the 1650s, he began preaching.

But England's political circumstances were changing. Following the restoration of Charles II in 1660, the government sought to reestablish religious uniformity under the Church of England.

Independent Protestant congregations faced increasing restrictions.

On November 12, 1660, Bunyan was arrested while attending a religious gathering at Lower Samsell, near Bedford.

He had been warned that authorities intended to arrest him but chose to attend anyway.

The government offered him a relatively simple way to regain his freedom: promise to stop preaching at unauthorized religious meetings.

Bunyan refused.

He would spend most of the next twelve years imprisoned.

The Preacher Who Would Not Be Silent

Bunyan's prosecution was not based upon accusations of violence or rebellion.

He was charged with participating in unlawful religious assemblies and refusing to conform to the established Church.

His case illustrates how closely religious conformity and political loyalty remained connected in seventeenth-century England.

The government feared that independent religious movements could destabilize the kingdom, particularly after the English Civil Wars and the execution of Charles I in 1649.

These concerns were not entirely imaginary. Religious divisions had contributed to decades of political upheaval.

Nevertheless, Bunyan's activities consisted principally of preaching and participating in religious gatherings.

In his autobiography, Grace Abounding to the Chief of Sinners, Bunyan described the circumstances of his arrest and imprisonment.

He explained that officials would not release him unless he agreed to abandon his preaching.

Bunyan believed he had received a responsibility from God that civil authorities could not legitimately require him to surrender.

He did not deny that government possessed lawful authority.

He denied that obedience to government required him to stop proclaiming the Gospel.

His resistance resembled the conviction expressed by the apostles in Acts 5:29:

“We ought to obey God rather than men.”

Yet Bunyan's story was not simply one of fearless defiance.

His writings reveal that imprisonment brought him considerable suffering.

text:
Trump wants data centers to make their own power and pay their neighbors. Developers have already promised the first part at scale. Very little of it is running.

On Wednesday the president wrote on Truth Social that new, large data centers are "mandated by me to make their own electricity," with any surplus sold back to the community or the grid. To win local support, he said, operators should pay residents a "dividend." Per Anadolu, the push builds on a voluntary pledge established in March. I can't find a rule that enforces it.

Cleanview, a research firm, counts 59 US data centers planning about 90 GW of their own behind-the-meter generation. As of mid-2026, about 2 GW was operating, or 2.2%. Another 1.2% was under construction, and 60% existed only as announcements. Part of that gap is timing: 92% of the pipeline was announced from 2025 on. Cleanview expects 2.8–3.2 GW online by the end of 2026.

Most of what runs, it says, belongs to xAI's Colossus sites outside Memphis: 1,498 MW of gas turbines, many of them temporary mobile units at a plant just across the state line in Southaven, Mississippi. On Tuesday Memphis's city council voted to halt construction of new data centers for 135 days, after a one-year moratorium failed, CBS reports.

Cleanview points to hardware and permits. Heavy-duty combined-cycle turbines are largely unavailable, so developers are buying truck-mounted generators, aeroderivative turbines and reciprocating engines. In New Jersey, it reports, Nebius is struggling to get an air permit for a 400 MW onsite gas plant; seven of the nine tranches in its $17.4 billion Microsoft deal depend on it. Nebius's revenue chief told CNBC a dividend was "not crazy to consider."

Cash has its own limits. In Hazle Township, Pennsylvania, the developer NorthPoint has offered, by letter, $10,000 to each of about 4,500 households once its first building runs, part of a $165 million community fund. Residents AFP spoke to called it a bribe. Residents had already won a court-ordered halt to construction and a township moratorium.

A dividend may buy consent in some towns. It cannot buy turbines, an air permit or a gas pipeline. Until far more than 2% of announced self-supply is actually generating, the grid, and the people who pay for it, remain the fallback.

text:
Elvis Presley's manager took up to 50% of what Elvis earned
The standard manager's cut in show business is 10–15%

1955. Elvis is 20. He's driving a truck in Memphis

He gets noticed by "Colonel" Tom Parker. A former carnival promoter. He was never a real colonel - it was an honorary title from a governor

Parker signs Elvis. And turns him into the King of Rock and Roll

Hollywood. Las Vegas. Hundreds of millions of records sold

But over time,Parker's cut keeps growing

From 1967, he takes 25% on movies and music. And 50% on every side deal: merchandise,souvenirs,special projects

1973. Parker sells RCA the royalty rights to Elvis's entire back catalog. More than 700 songs. For $5.4 million

He takes half for himself

Elvis will never earn another cent from those songs

Parker in the video below, asked about taking "half":
"My deal was not 50% of the profit. On the motion pictures,the hotel and the music business - 25%. Never no more. All I know is I sleep very good at night"

The case for Parker: without him,Elvis might have stayed a truck driver. Parker cut the deals,built the career,made the name. And Elvis renewed his contract again and again

1977. Elvis dies at 42

A court reviews his finances. The estate's guardian calls Parker's deals "excessive" and against Elvis's interests. In 1983,Parker agrees to cut all ties with the Presley estate

And at the end of the interview,he turns the question back on the reporter:
"Do you think I exploited him as much as he exploited me?"

In his entire career,Elvis never played a single concert in Europe. He was offered millions

Parker said Elvis "didn't want to go"

The truth: Parker was an illegal immigrant from the Netherlands. He had no passport. If he left the US,he might never have been allowed back in

Did Parker earn his money - or rob Elvis?

text:
WITKOFF IN ST PETERSBURG: A PEACE PLAN TO ‘ANALYSE’, DIESEL FUEL TO DELIVER

Witkoff arrived in St Petersburg carrying a peace plan. He left with a promise of diesel deliveries. After nearly three hours at the Konstantinovsky Palace, one thing is clear: the Kremlin will ‘analyse’ the documentation, talks about talks will take place in November, and tankers will sail from Russian ports.

There is no peace. There is a timetable.

🔹 Who, where, how long

21 October, Strelna outside St Petersburg. Nearly three hours.

At the table sat Putin, his adviser Yuri Ushakov and Kirill Dmitriev. Dmitriev is Putin’s economic envoy — in other words, a full-time salesman for the vision of ‘great joint business opportunities’. Jared Kushner joined remotely.

A day earlier in Oslo, the Americans had consulted the package with Ukraine and Europe. Putin was therefore presented with an ‘updated’ version.

🔹 What was in the documentation

No one has published the full text. Reports by Reuters, AP and Axios give us the scope of the discussions:

▪️ a ceasefire, including partial arrangements covering energy and food security;
▪️ the status of the occupied territories;
▪️ security guarantees;
▪️ post-war reconstruction;
▪️ a new security architecture for Europe.
Details of any territorial compromise remain unclear.
The best point of reference is the proposal by Witkoff and Kushner described by David Ignatius in The Washington Post on 12 October. It was developed on 9 October during a six-hour meeting at the Shell Bay golf club in Florida.
After all, where else would one draw the borders of Europe if not on a golf course?
Four pillars:

1️⃣ Reconstruction of Ukraine with the participation of the World Bank and BlackRock. This would include infrastructure, the economy and payments to the families of those killed and wounded, together with anti-corruption safeguards.

2️⃣ US and European security guarantees ‘in the style of NATO’s Article 5’. In return, Russia would negotiate separate agreements with Europe concerning its own security demands.

Ukraine has already received one document containing security assurances: the 1994 Budapest Memorandum. Russia signed that one too.

3️⃣ The return of Russian oil and gas to the EU market, including through pipelines, with Kyiv sharing the profits with Moscow. There would also be a timetable for lifting sanctions.

Ukraine would become a business partner of the state that has spent years bombing its energy infrastructure.

4️⃣ Freezing the conflict along the front line. Russia would retain de facto control over the occupied territories, including the part of Donbas it currently holds, while abandoning claims to the remaining areas. There would be no legal recognition of the annexations.

Caveat: there is no independent confirmation that this exact proposal was discussed on 21 October. Its elements, however, correspond to the scope of the talks in Oslo.

🔹 What Putin offered

Fact: Russia will ‘in principle’ return to trilateral Russia–Ukraine–US talks after 10 November. Expert teams would meet first, followed perhaps by the leaders. According to Ushakov, the subject would be post-war security arrangements for Russia and Ukraine.

No specific date was agreed.

Fact: the plan was not accepted. Peskov said the proposals would be ‘analysed’ and described the talks as ‘substantive’.

Assessment: in the Kremlin’s vocabulary, ‘we will analyse it’ does not mean ‘yes’. It means: let us see how much more we can squeeze out of this.

Fact: Moscow’s position on an energy ceasefire ‘has not changed’, according to Peskov.

That same day, Witkoff told Putin about ‘progress towards a ceasefire’.

🔹 Donbas: the heart of the matter

Zelenskyy told Fox News on 21 October that he is prepared to freeze the war along the current front line. A ceasefire is the absolute minimum, and it must be accompanied by security guarantees.

Moscow is demanding the whole of Donetsk Oblast and Ukraine’s exclusion from NATO. Lavrov warned before the meeting that there would be no political concessions in exchange for economic benefits.

Peskov said this morning that the ‘Ukrainian problem’ cannot be resolved without ‘someone from Kyiv’, because ‘someone there has to make a responsible decision’.

Translated from Kremlin-speak: a ‘responsible decision’ means surrendering the rest of Donbas without a fight.

And whom is Washington pressuring?

According to Axios, Kushner once again demanded in Oslo that Kyiv halt strikes on Russian refineries.

Zelenskyy’s answer: ‘Go ahead, if Russia commits to doing the same.’

The pressure exists. It is simply directed at one side.

🔹 Peace in the briefcase, business on the table

Putin presented his own offer:

▪️ restoration of economic cooperation with the United States;
▪️ ‘large quantities of fertiliser for the American market’;
▪️ a meeting with Trump in China in November, on neutral ground provided by his ‘no limits’ friend;
▪️ Russian mediation on Iran.

The recipient of Iranian Shahed drones is offering to mediate on Iran.

Witkoff responded with praise. He said the Americans were working ‘very well’ with Mr Dmitriev and that the US Treasury was already working with him on agreements.

As Witkoff put it, Washington is ‘openly discussing’ with Ukraine the opportunities that ‘may open up for it’ after the war.

In the proposal described by The Washington Post, Russia was offered something rather more concrete: a timetable for lifting sanctions.
🔹 Diesel. Let’s check it
Putin claims that following the diesel agreement, prices on global markets fell by 5–6 per cent.
Several tankers are supposedly awaiting dispatch. The first is to sail within two or three days carrying 40,000 tonnes, with others following ‘one after another’.

The White House envoy thanked the aggressor because the diesel ‘could help American farmers and truck drivers’.

Let’s check that.

After Trump announced the agreement, crude oil and diesel futures fell by roughly 2–4 per cent, not 5–6 per cent. There was no lasting effect on retail prices.

The market is facing fuel shortages caused by the war in the Middle East, while prices at the pump remain extremely high.

Putin exaggerated the effect of his ‘gift’ by roughly a factor of two.

Business as usual.

🔹 The only tangible result

Stephen Hubbard, an American held by Russia since 2022, has been released.

Washington stresses that there was no prisoner exchange.

It is good that he is going home.

But this is a gesture, not progress.

Hostage diplomacy in its purest form: first you seize someone, then you ‘return’ them as an act of goodwill.

🔹 Conclusion

Witkoff presented a negotiating proposal, not a treaty.

Russia left the door open to another round of talks, but on Donbas it did not move an inch.

There is also one small detail Washington prefers to overlook.

Returning Russian raw materials to the EU market requires Europe’s consent.

Yet on the very same day, Peskov complained that Europe’s common position, reiterated by Finnish President Alexander Stubb, was ‘unlikely to make a constructive contribution’.

You can promise Moscow access to the European market.

You can no longer deliver it without Europe.

The Kremlin was not selling peace in St Petersburg.

It was buying time — and paying for it in diesel.

text:
In 2026, because of the Meta Andromeda update...

If your ads aren't profitable, it's likely not a targeting issue, it's a messaging issue. Lemme explain...

Meta is incentivized to get your ads to the right people. They want people to stay on the platform and get value.

So it's not that you're not getting to the right people - it's that you're not saying the right things.

When we analyze ad accounts for our clients, the biggest lift is improving the copywriting of the ads.

Here's how we rebuild messaging from scratch (I call this the 6P's of copyTHINKING):

• People. Who is your offer for?
• Positioning. Why you over anyone else?
• Promise. What do they get?
• Proof. Why trust you?
• Priority. Why act now?
• Process. How does it work?

1. People

You can't answer "why should they choose us?" until you answer "who is they?"

Let’s say you’re selling a marathon training program.

The messaging will be different depending on who your avatar is.

Someone who's never run before vs. A busy professional vs. A runner over 40 vs. Someone chasing a Boston qualifier vs. Someone coming back from an injury.

2. Positioning

Positioning = how your product is perceived in the consumer's mind.

Why this matters:
• Increases brand recognition
• Lubricates sales process
• Makes it easier for others to talk about you

Seth Godin once wrote, “Successful brands are built with your customers talking about you, not you talking about you...Marketing is about creating the conditions for other people to eagerly spread your idea.”

How to do research to nail your positioning:

• Out (competitors)
• In (your features)
• Forward (what customers value)

3. Promise

Aka what do they get?

It’s not features/deliverables. Where are you helping them get to? Who are they trying to become?

Steve Jobs didn’t say “5 gigabytes of storage” he said “1,000 songs in your pocket.”

EXERCISE: the “so what?” test

If you’re selling a rug you might say, "This is a 10-by-5-foot rug made from llama wool."

So what?

"It's large enough to anchor your living room."

So what?

"Your room feels pulled together rather than random."

So what?

"When people walk in, you get compliments."

So what?

"You feel like someone with great taste and a home worth showing off."

Now we're talking :)

4. Proof

Proof = evidence that backs the promise.

Trust is belief with evidence. Belief without evidence is called faith.

There are 3 types proof:

1/ Authority by association (Elon Musk says “XYZ”)
2/ Your results (I went from making $8/hr as a barista to buying my literal dream home because of high ticket sales)
3/ Client results (This is Sabrina. She went from making $50,000/year as a teacher to $50,000/month as a HTS closer)

Key point: Proof is relative. You want to match the proof to the avatar.

A case study from a 50 year old asian woman will be more persuasive to other middle-aged asian ladies.

A case study from a 21 year old kid from Florida will be more persuasive to other young people in their 20s.

5. Priority

There are only two reasons people act now:
1/ Go toward something pleasurable
2/ Or run away from something painful

I prefer to use PAIN rather than PLEASURE because we will jog toward pleasure but we will SPRINT from pain.

Highlight the cost of inaction. (aka what happens if you stay on this path??)

6. Process

Process = an explanation for how you get results.

If I said "We’ll help you lose weight", that can be achieved through many different processes.

• Calorie counting
• Fasting
• GLP-1
• Pilates

A good process does 4 things:

(1) explains why other solutions fail
(2) creates a believable path
(3) feels different
(4) is easy to understand.

Alright, those are the 6Ps:

People: who is your offer for?
Positioning: why you over others?
Promise: what do they get?
Proof: why trust you?
Priority: why act now?
Process: how does it work?

Happy ad writing :)

- Jay

Ps. I write ads for the BIGGEST info offers in the game (just ask around). If you want me to write your ads for your info offer, DM me. Cheers!

Trump did say the words attributed to him. At an Oct. 20, 2026, rally in Greenville, North Carolina, he stated that if Republicans win the House and Senate, he is “directing the Department of Justice to settle all remaining legitimate claims as soon as possible,” adding: “If we don’t win, there’s no money. If we do win, you’re getting it.” He also claimed his administration had already delivered about $1 billion in settlements and said the funds should go to families rather than lawyers.⁠Forbes

The stronger claim that he will “deny” claims or medical treatment if Republicans lose is an interpretation, not a direct quote. The Camp Lejeune Justice Act (part of the 2022 PACT Act signed by Biden) created the legal path for these claims. Settlements are paid from the permanent Judgment Fund, which does not require new congressional appropriations. DOJ has continued and accelerated offers under Trump; as of mid-September 2026, offers exceeded $1.1 billion with roughly $879 million paid. Legal rights under the Act remain in place regardless of the midterms.⁠Justice

What Trump explicitly conditioned on a GOP win is a directive to speed up settlement of the remaining backlog (hundreds of thousands of claims filed, only a small fraction resolved so far). Executive control over settlement pace is real, but the underlying statutory rights and funding mechanism are not election-contingent. The remarks frame ongoing resolution as dependent on election outcomes, which is the factual core of the controversy.

text:
[Why do Japanese AI companies end up doing contract development and implementation support, unlike their American and Chinese counterparts?]
I think a major dividing line is whether people can give an underestimated technology enough time and money to prove itself.
America has plenty of prejudice against new ideas too. But when one person dismisses an idea, someone else can still bet on it.
Writing this off as a lack of talent or ambition among Japanese engineers is far too simplistic.

===================================
[Contract work is a rational choice]

If you help a large company adopt AI, there is a customer ready to pay.

If you build your own product or develop a model at the frontier of AI, you have to spend heavily before knowing whether anyone will buy it.

The first business pays salaries today.

The second can burn through years of funding before it finds a market.

Under those conditions, choosing contract work is perfectly rational.

Telling founders to "be more ambitious" does not pay their employees.

Preferred Networks is one company trying to go further.

It develops its own AI models and specialized chips, while also turning research into services such as Matlantis for materials discovery.

But the funding gap is staggering.

The funding round it announced in April 2025 totaled JPY 24 billion, including equity and loans.

OpenAI announced a USD 40 billion round the previous month.

At JPY 150 to the dollar, that is JPY 6 trillion.

A difference of roughly 250 times.

These are fundraising figures, not annual research budgets, but they show the scale of the resources available.

And SoftBank led that OpenAI round.

Japan clearly has money.

The question is whether that money connects with researchers, founders and businesses in a way that lets a Japanese company grow to that scale.

===================================
[Japan had both technical talent and capital]

This connects to the earlier question: "Why did Japan not produce an NVIDIA?"

Sega and Namco developed sophisticated graphics hardware and made money with it.

Sega even worked with NVIDIA in its early years.

Japan was not watching the whole thing from the sidelines.

At Sony, Ken Kutaragi pushed the Cell processor project with Toshiba and IBM.

His vision extended beyond a game console to computing across home electronics and servers.

There was ambition, engineering talent and substantial investment.

But powerful hardware alone does not create a platform.

Other developers need tools that make the hardware useful without requiring them to become specialists in every detail of its design.

NVIDIA expanded from games into scientific computing and AI while building that broader developer environment.

The difference was not simply who could design an impressive chip.

It was also who could turn that chip into something that thousands of other people could build businesses on.

-----------------------------------
[Universities had promising research too]

Japan's LINKS-1 computer graphics system was completed in 1982.

Its technology helped produce imagery for the 1985 Tsukuba Expo.

Researchers such as Tomoyuki Nishita and Eihachiro Nakamae were also working on realistic lighting methods around the same period as leading American researchers.

Japan did not lack the seeds.

Meanwhile, Silicon Graphics emerged from Stanford and secured backing to turn university research into a business.

LINKS-1 and Silicon Graphics were not identical products.

Still, the comparison raises an important question.

Who would fund the next step, recruit a management team and help sell the technology beyond its original setting?

A brilliant prototype does not automatically become a global company.

Someone has to finance the messy stretch in between.

===================================
[Apple's success helped keep Pixar alive]

Steve Jobs could support Pixar because he had already made his fortune at Apple.

In 1986, he put USD 10 million into the newly independent company.

His total investment eventually reached roughly USD 50 million.

Pixar tried selling computers and software, made short films and took on commercial work.

It did not start with a guaranteed hit called Toy Story.

Jobs could keep financing the company while its people worked out what the technology could become.

[One success bought time for the next technology.]

That matters enormously.

Pixar also brought together computer graphics research and the storytelling skills of people such as John Lasseter.

Better images alone would not have made audiences care about its characters.

And Pixar itself did contract work.

So the issue is not whether a company accepts contracts.

It is whether that work helps it accumulate technology and experience that it can eventually turn into products of its own.

If every project ends with handing everything over to a client, the company has to start selling its time again.

===================================
[America has prejudice and bureaucracy too]

Neural networks were not always fashionable.

There were long periods when many researchers doubted their usefulness.

Geoffrey Hinton's work also benefited from support in Canada.

This was never a story in which American private investors alone recognized every important idea.

New technologies are often awkward, unreliable and easy to laugh at.

Sometimes the criticism is justified.

But "it does not work well yet" and "it will never be useful" are very different judgments.

The real question is whether researchers can keep experimenting long enough to find out which one is true.

-----------------------------------
[Letting a small experiment change the company's direction]

Alec Radford's experiments were an important part of the path toward GPT.

Sam Altman helped turn promising research into a much larger effort, with Microsoft providing crucial backing.

The research mattered.

So did the decision to commit resources when the evidence became compelling.

Claude Code also began as a side project by Boris Cherny in September 2024.

A small experiment became a major product.

By May 2026, Anthropic said Claude was writing more than 80 percent of the new code merged into its production systems.

That does not mean the company had become a fully autonomous machine that could improve itself without people.

Humans still set goals, review results and make decisions.

But it does show how far a seemingly small experiment can go when a company gives it room and resources.

Can a young engineer's results change where the company puts its money?

Or must the engineer spend years persuading people whose careers depend on the existing plan?

That difference can decide the outcome.

Google also had to respond.

After ChatGPT, it brought Google Brain and DeepMind together and developed Gemini.

Meta has likewise reorganized its AI effort under Alexandr Wang and pushed forward with models such as Muse Wonder.

Even wealthy American companies can become slow and bureaucratic.

What matters is whether they can change course.

===================================
[People can move across institutional boundaries]

Stanford's role is another important part of this story.

Fei-Fei Li helped establish ImageNet.

Andrew Ng helped bring machine learning education to a huge audience through online courses and Coursera.

Their careers also offered visible examples of what people with Chinese backgrounds could achieve in AI.

It is reasonable to think that such examples encouraged others, even if their precise influence is difficult to measure.

But the broader point is the movement of people and knowledge.

University research reaches companies.

People with industrial experience return to research, start businesses or fund the next generation.

If companies dismiss academics as people who know nothing about the real world, they cut themselves off from part of that process.

Lauren Tan, known online as @poteto, offers a more recent example.

She worked on projects including React Compiler at Meta, moved to Cursor and subsequently joined the Grok effort through the acquisition.

Her work included teaching coding agents to inspect performance problems and help improve software.

An acquisition can transfer far more than a product.

It can move people who know how to make difficult technology work.

And when people have several places to take their ideas, one employer's judgment does not have to decide their future.

===================================
[China built a different route]

China's development followed a different combination of forces.

There were exchanges with American universities and companies.

There was also a large domestic education and research base.

And there was an enormous home market in which companies could grow.

Restrictions on foreign internet services helped create room for domestic businesses.

But protection alone does not explain everything.

Taobao competed against eBay in China and won.

Chinese companies still had to build services that customers wanted.

Once firms such as Alibaba and ByteDance became large, they could become sources of capital themselves.

Alibaba invested USD 800 million in Moonshot AI.

Public investment funds added another source of money.

China therefore developed several routes through which resources could reach new AI companies.

DeepSeek's early development illustrates another route.

The financial success of High-Flyer helped fund a new AI effort.

Again, an earlier success financed a new technical bet.

That describes DeepSeek's origins, rather than a claim that it has remained entirely self-funded.

Japan cannot simply copy China's internet controls.

Nor should supporting domestic technology require copying censorship.

Funding research, expanding access to computing and helping companies grow are separate policy choices.

===================================
[A route Japan may have lost]

Takafumi Horie's Livedoor was trying to expand through acquisitions and the stock market.

Its acquisitions included technology companies such as Turbolinux.

For a small startup, being acquired can be an important way for its founders, employees and investors to realize the value they have created.

Those people can then invest in or start another company.

That possibility also makes it easier for investors to back a startup in the first place.

If Livedoor had survived and continued developing, it might have become a larger source of funding and acquisition opportunities.

That is a possibility worth considering.

It is not proof that Livedoor would have become a Japanese Google.

Nor can anyone establish that it would eventually have bought Preferred Networks and financed an OpenAI-scale research program.

Still, the question should not be brushed aside.

Holding people accountable for wrongdoing and examining the wider economic consequences of an enforcement action are compatible.

A country can punish misconduct while also asking whether its institutions unnecessarily destroyed opportunities for future investment.

-----------------------------------
[Blaming contract developers gets us nowhere]

Not every AI company needs to develop a frontier model.

Helping businesses use AI has real value.

Contract development is not a disgrace.

The problem is when it becomes the only practical way for talented people to survive.

If the system rewards work that can be billed immediately, companies will organize around that work.

If an ambitious project fails to find funding, telling its founders that they lacked courage is a pretty convenient excuse.

The American advantage is not that everyone welcomes new ideas.

It is that a rejected idea can sometimes find another investor, another company or another wealthy founder willing to take a chance.

Japan has produced exceptional engineers and ambitious entrepreneurs too.

I do not think the answer is to wait for another extraordinary individual to fight through everything alone.

We need more ways for those people to keep going.

[When one person says no, someone else must still be able to place a bet.]

That is the kind of system I think Japan needs to build.

text:
Utah’s Kalshi Lawsuit Raises the State-vs.-Federal Stakes

Utah’s effort to halt Kalshi’s operations is the day’s clearest signal that the legal fight over prediction markets is moving from theory into state-by-state enforcement. Axios reports that Attorney General Derek Brown has sued Kalshi, arguing over a question that will shape the industry’s expansion: are event contracts federally regulated derivatives, or gambling products that states can regulate themselves?

Utah presses the jurisdiction fight

The Utah case puts Kalshi’s operating model under direct pressure in another state. The core dispute is not merely about one platform’s availability; it is about which regulator gets the final word as prediction markets seek wider adoption.

For market participants, the outcome could influence where platforms can offer contracts, how quickly they expand, and whether state-level legal challenges become a recurring cost of doing business. A favorable result for Utah could embolden other states to test similar arguments. A favorable result for Kalshi would strengthen the case that federally overseen event contracts sit outside conventional state gambling frameworks.

Polymarket removes criticized Cornell contract

In a separate test of industry boundaries, the Associated Press reports that Polymarket removed a market asking whether Cornell students accused of sexual assault would face felony charges. The contract drew criticism before it was taken down.

The episode underscores a different risk facing prediction-market operators: reputational and governance pressure. Even when a contract can technically be listed, platforms still have to decide where to draw lines around sensitive real-world events, especially when markets involve alleged crimes and identifiable people. Content standards, moderation decisions, and response speed are becoming meaningful parts of platform credibility.

A busier market, with bigger scrutiny

The market-pulse data shows activity remains broad, spanning 2026 midterm control, a Federal Reserve decision, and a major soccer match. That mix illustrates why prediction markets are attracting attention beyond traditional sports betting: they increasingly sit at the intersection of politics, economics, and live events.

But broader relevance also brings a wider set of stakeholders—state officials, federal regulators, users, critics, and institutions—each with different expectations for how these platforms should operate.

Why it matters

Today’s developments show the industry facing two simultaneous tests: legal authority and editorial judgment. Utah’s lawsuit could affect the regulatory map for event-contract platforms, while Polymarket’s removal highlights the practical limits platforms may impose even absent a formal rule. For followers of these markets, regulatory access and contract-selection policies may matter as much as the prices on the screen.

text:
》》》》》

I wanted to be closer to him.

I wanted a look that belonged to me, not simply the kindness he offered to everyone who crossed his path.

I wanted to be the person he remembered at the end of a long, exhausting day.

The person he reached for without thinking when something important threatened to slip away.

And someday, perhaps—

I wanted him to show me the parts of himself he never allowed anyone else to see.

I wanted him to trust me with the loneliness he never spoke about, with the exhaustion he disguised as composure, with the feelings he kept tucked behind that carefully controlled expression.

If he had spent so long protecting other people that he had forgotten what it meant to be protected himself, I wanted to remind him.

Again and again.

That he didn't have to carry everything alone.

That he was allowed to rest.

That before he was the man who saved others, before he was the doctor everyone depended on, before he was the person who always seemed to know what needed to be done, he was simply a man who deserved to be cared for, too.

I wished I could tell him that.

I wished I could become someone who did not merely give him another reason to worry, someone who was not simply another person he felt responsible for protecting.

I wanted to become one of the places he could return to.

One of the places where he didn't have to be strong.

I traced the edge of the notebook with my fingertips.

I wanted so many things.

And yet, whenever I was standing in front of him, I couldn't bring myself to say even one of them.

I love you.

Three little words.

Why did I spend so much of my time thinking about how not to trouble him?

Why did I search for ways to make it easier for him to reject me before I had even given him the chance to answer?

Perhaps I was afraid.

Afraid that my feelings might disturb the quiet balance of our relationship.

Afraid that I might destroy something precious simply because I wanted to name it.

And more than anything, afraid that I would discover I was not as special to him as he had become to me.

I let out a slow breath.

Moonlight fell across the notebook, softening the white paper into something almost silver.

The moon was far away.

No matter how long I reached for it, I would never be able to touch it.

I didn't know how to cross the distance between us.

And yet people kept looking up at the moon.

They made wishes beneath its light, knowing perfectly well that it could never hear them.

Perhaps love was like that.

Perhaps it wasn't always about whether a feeling could be returned, or whether it could reach the person it was meant for.

Perhaps sometimes it was simply the unbearable happiness of knowing that someone existed in the same world as you.

The quiet wish that their tomorrow might be gentler than their today.

The hope that they would never have to face a lonely night without something warm to hold on to.

The desire to see them happy, even if your own name never became part of that happiness.

I wished I could love him that way.

I wished I could be content with wanting nothing in return.

But I wasn't that strong.

I still wanted him to love me.

I wanted him to say that he loved me, too.

I wanted to wake beside him and hear his voice before the day began.

I wanted to sit across from him over an ordinary meal, share the same view, laugh at something meaningless, and discover the small, unremarkable happiness of being part of his everyday life.

I didn't need a miracle.

I didn't need a grand confession beneath a sky full of stars.

I wanted to belong somewhere in the ordinary hours of his life.

Even if I could only be a single sentence in the long story of his existence, I wanted to become a sentence he would never forget.

I wasn't ready to let go of that wish.

So I lowered my eyes and continued writing.

Zayne, what are you doing right now?

Perhaps he was still working.

》》》》》

The Biafra Self-Referendum: Organizing Independence from Exile Under International Law

In a detailed response to public questions, the Alliance of Biafran Americans explained the mechanics and legitimacy of a self-referendum for Biafran independence organized by PM Simon Ekpa and the Biafra Republic Government in Exile (BRGIE). 

It stated that the process was not an ad-hoc online exercise but one conducted both physically in the claimed Biafran homeland and electronically among the diaspora. It asserted that #Biafrans themselves authorized Ekpa to lead the effort after electing him Prime Minister at an assembly in Helsinki, Finland, in 2023.

The referendum is presented as a response to long-standing grievances. 

The accompanying quoted statement of Dr. Michael Rubin @mrubin1971 noted that

“Nigerian repression grew against ethnic Igbo in Biafra and Nigerian Christians more broadly,” framing the vote as an exercise of self-determination amid allegations of marginalization, insecurity, and ineffective governance. 

Organizers reported that tens of millions participated and overwhelmingly chose independence, with plans for a convention to declare the “Restoration of Independence of Biafra.” 

Dr. Rubin emphasized that holding aspects of the process in #Finland is not disqualifying, drawing a parallel to Czechoslovakia’s 1918 declaration of independence, which took place in Washington, D.C., rather than on Czech or Slovak soil.

On verification and international standards, the PAC stated that ORB International monitored the process on the ground and published a report. 

It further argued that United Nations involvement is not a legal prerequisite for a referendum on self-determination. While a state or entity may invite the UN, international law does not mandate it. 

ORB’s published commentary focused on public-opinion polling showing that residents of Biafra regions were among the most likely to view the national government as ineffective and to report feeling unsafe, providing contextual support for the organizers’ stated motivations even if it did not independently audit every ballot.

Under the 1933 Montevideo Convention on the Rights and Duties of States, an entity may claim the attributes of statehood by possessing a permanent population, a defined territory, a government, and the capacity to enter into relations with other states. 

Article 3 of the Convention codifies the declarative theory: “The political existence of the state is independent of recognition by the other states.” 

Proponents of Biafran independence argue that a credible expression of popular will—through a referendum—helps demonstrate the existence of a permanent population seeking self-government and can support claims of an effective government and capacity for external relations, even if full international recognition remains a separate political question. 

Recognition is ultimately a discretionary act by existing states; meeting the Montevideo criteria is widely treated as a necessary but not always sufficient condition.

#Somaliland offers a relevant comparative example. After declaring independence in 1991, Somaliland held a constitutional referendum on 31 May 2001. Approximately 97 percent of those who voted approved the constitution, which affirmed independence. An international observer team from the Initiative and Referendum Institute concluded that the process was conducted “openly, fairly, honestly, and largely in accordance with internationally recognized election procedures,” despite limited participation in some contested areas. 

Somaliland has since maintained a functioning government, defined borders roughly corresponding to the former British Somaliland, and a permanent population, meeting the core Montevideo criteria in practice.

text:
The Brothers Karamazov：
It is easy to love humanity in the abstract, and almost unbearable to love a single human being up close in a small room for twenty-four hours. That confession, delivered early in The Brothers Karamazov and examined by Elder Zosima, might be the sharpest diagnostic scalpel Fyodor Dostoevsky ever held up to the modern soul. We spend so much time discussing this novel as a grand battlefield between faith and atheism that we often miss the more intimate, uncomfortable territory where the battle actually takes place: the gap between our lofty philosophical ideals and our revulsion toward the actual, smelly, foolish people standing right in front of us.

What lingers longest after finishing the book is not the murder mystery at its center, nor even the famous theological debates treated in isolation, but the sheer, claustrophobic difficulty these characters have in simply tolerating one another’s existence.

Consider Ivan Karamazov. In a tavern smelling of sour beer and cheap tobacco, he builds the most devastating case against God in Western literature. He does not argue that God does not exist; he argues that a universe built on the unredeemed tears of a single tortured five-year-old girl is a moral obscenity, and he respectfully returns his ticket of admission. Intellectually, Ivan is unassailable. Any honest reader feels the pull of his outrage. And yet, watch what happens the moment Ivan leaves the realm of universal justice and steps back into his father’s house.

He cannot bear the sound of his father’s footsteps on the floor below. He cannot stand the vulgar, servile familiarity of his half-brother Smerdyakov. Ivan is capable of weeping over the suffering of distant children he has never met, while simultaneously listening on the staircase in a state of paralyzed, half-conscious complicity as his own father moves toward murder. Smerdyakov becomes Ivan’s nightmare not because Smerdyakov is a monster, but because he is a literalist. He takes Ivan’s elegant philosophical despair and translates it into a heavy iron paperweight crushed against an old man’s skull. Dostoevsky is relentless here: he shows us how easily high-minded moral disgust with the world curdles into permission to despise the flawed individuals who inhabit it.

Against Ivan’s cold clarity stands Dmitri, a man who is almost entirely appetite, impulse, and public humiliation. On paper, Dmitri should be insufferable. He is violent, financially reckless, cruel to Katerina Ivanovna, and consumed by a feverish obsession with Grushenka. Yet Dmitri possesses something Ivan lacks entirely: he never pretends to be cleaner than the mud he is standing in. When Dmitri is interrogated in the village of Mokroye, stripped of his clothes down to his dirty socks while officials dissect every shameful detail of his debt and his temper, he experiences a strange awakening through his dream of the "wee one"—the starving baby in the burned-out peasant village. Dmitri does not ask why God permits the baby to freeze; he simply asks why people are poor and why nobody helps them, and immediately accepts that he is somehow responsible for all of it.

And then there is Alyosha, whom Dostoevsky intended as the hero of the book, though he is perhaps the hardest character for a modern mind to understand. We tend to mistake Alyosha for a passive saint, a gentle mediator who floats above his brothers’ chaos. Look closer at the crucial turning point of his story: the death of his beloved mentor, Elder Zosima.

Everyone in the monastery expects a miracle when Zosima dies; they expect his body to remain incorrupt and emit the fragrance of holiness. Instead, Zosima’s corpse begins to rot and stink faster than normal in the summer heat. For Alyosha, this is a crisis that mirrors Ivan’s rebellion. Why would Providence allow the holiest man he knew to be humiliated by the crudest physical laws of putrefaction? Alyosha’s faith is saved not by a theological argument, and not by an angel, but by Grushenka offering him what she calls a single "onion"—a tiny, unexpected act of human tenderness when she realizes his heart is breaking. When Alyosha falls to the earth outside the monastery afterward, weeping and kissing the ground, he is no longer worshipping a pristine, miraculous God who overrides nature. He is accepting the world as it actually is, complete with the smell of decay.

That is the quiet counter-argument Dostoevsky offers to Ivan’s "Grand Inquisitor." The Inquisitor believes human beings are too weak for freedom; they want bread, certainty, and someone to take the burden of conscience away from them. He may even be right about human history. Neither Christ in the poem nor Dostoevsky in the novel ever refutes the Inquisitor with words. The only answer offered is a silent kiss on the old man’s bloodless ninety-year-old lips—a refusal to argue, a refusal to coerce, and a stubborn insistence on remaining present with the person who is condemning you.

We still live inside the Karamazov family house. We have never been better at Ivan’s kind of love—fierce, articulate, righteous outrage on behalf of humanity from a safe distance. And we have never been more terrified of Zosima’s kind of love, which requires looking at an irritating, contradictory, unredeemed neighbor without turning away. At the very end of the book, standing by young Ilyusha’s grave with a group of boys, Alyosha does not promise them that they will grow up to be great or sinless men. He only asks that they hold onto one good memory from childhood, because a single warm memory of being loved without calculation might one day keep them from doing something terrible when the world turns dark. It seems almost laughably small compared to the cosmic trial of God that came before it, until you realize that in Dostoevsky’s world, a single onion is the only thing that ever actually pulls anyone out of hell.

Personal Manifesto: Pragmatic Zionism

I am an atheist and anticlerical, humanist and liberal, antifascist and anticommunist. From this position, I defend Israel's right to exist as a sovereign state, just as I defend the right of Pakistan, Bangladesh, Kuwait, and Kosovo to exist, even though they all came into being through partitions, wars, and displacement. I am not ashamed of this. If that makes me a Zionist, then so be it, and I am a pragmatic one.

Zionism, in its basic sense, is the affirmation of the self-determination of the Jewish people in a land with which they maintain a millennia-old historical bond. It requires neither religious faith nor loyalty to any specific government. Israel is a state with secular institutions, a parliamentary system, and minorities; its Jewish national character does not make it a theocracy nor does it invalidate its legitimacy. Denying this right to exist while recognizing the right of other states born in similar circumstances is a double standard that I do not accept.

I do not support Hamas or its acolytes. Hamas is an Islamist movement whose stated goal has been, and remains, the destruction of Israel. The attack of October 7, 2023, with the deliberate killing of civilians, rapes, and kidnappings, was not an act of legitimate resistance: it was a planned crime. Criticizing the Palestinian cause “as it stands”—dominated for decades by the rejection of partition offers and by prioritizing “resistance” over building a viable state—is not whitewashing anything. It is pointing to a pattern of political failure. Nor do I support the Palestinian Authority in its current form, the BDS movement, or initiatives like the so-called Freedom Flotilla, whose real objective is often the delegitimization of Israel rather than a negotiated resolution.

That does not mean I support settlements or the policies of Netanyahu or figures like Ben Gvir. Settlement expansion complicates any territorial agreement and creates unnecessary friction. Netanyahu has his own political and legal responsibilities; I owe him no loyalty. Criticizing those policies is compatible with defending the existence and security of the state. They are separate issues.

My position on resolving the conflict is pragmatic: a two-state solution structured through a binational confederation, with a shared capital in Jerusalem. Two sovereign states that recognize each other, with defined borders, joint institutions where necessary (security, resources, holy sites), and regulated freedom of movement. It is neither a utopia nor a surrender: it is an attempt to recognize the legitimacy of both national aspirations without demanding the disappearance of one of them. Territorial maximalism on one side and the total rejection of the other's existence on the opposing side have proven unworkable.

Accusations of "whitewashing genocide" for not supporting Hamas or for defending Israel's right to exist do not impress me. The term genocide has a precise legal meaning that requires a specific intent to destroy a group as such. The high number of civilian casualties in urban warfare against an enemy that deliberately embeds itself within the population is a real and grave tragedy, but it does not automatically negate a state's right to defend itself, nor does it transform any defense of its existence into complicity. I apply the same standard to other conflicts.

- Lux Rationis

text:
The figure behind Mesmero

Magneto's presence hangs over this whole operation. His name carries authority with the Demi-Men, Mesmero answers to him, and Lorna is asked to accept him as her father. When he appears, the X-Men have every reason to take the threat seriously.

There is a catch that matters when keeping these early groups straight. X-Men #58 reveals that the Magneto connected to Mesmero and the Demi-Men was a robot. So this belongs to the history of a group operating under Magneto's image, not another version of his original Brotherhood.

Within the #49–52 adventure, that image is enough. Mesmero treats it as a source of power. Lorna feels an obligation to it. Cyclops uses the chain of command to work his way inside under the Erik the Red disguise.

The promise made to Lorna is also much more calculated than an invitation to join a team. She is offered a throne beside him and told to think of her powers as a reason to rule. Her resemblance to him in what she can do becomes evidence in a story about who she ought to be.

Then there is the way the operation ends. When Lorna refuses the role he has assigned her, the supposed patriarch abandons the base and leaves it set to explode. All that talk of loyalty and family ends with the people inside having to get themselves out. Bobby's ice protects the escaping group from the blast.

It is a strange little chapter in the original run, but it introduces a character who will matter far beyond these soldiers and their hidden city. The army falls apart. Lorna's story is only getting started.

text:
Historically, a “cold harbor” was lodging that offered a traveler shelter but no food. The word “harbor” itself reaches back to the Old English herebeorg—the “here-” prefix meaning “army,” and beorg, “shelter.” At the infamous Civil War Battle of Cold Harbor in 1864, entrenched Confederate defenses stopped a disastrous Union assault. Earlier, Lee had repeatedly failed to check Grant’s advance toward Richmond, but at Cold Harbor his entrenchments held. However the victory could not ultimately stop Grant from changing the battlefield. Unable to continue towards Richmond, he moved around Lee, crossed the James River, and struck at Petersburg, the supply route to Richmond. Cold Harbor was Lee’s last major field victory: his army had found a position it could defend, but not one from which it could regain the initiative. The name of the battle apparently was not a metaphor, but a literal reference to a nearby crossroads at which there was an Inn where people could shelter that didn’t serve any hot food.

The Battle of Cold Harbor is remembered chiefly for the slaughter of Union troops attacking Lee’s entrenched line and for Grant’s later admission that the attack was a mistake.[136] “I have always regretted that the last assault at Cold Harbor was ever made,” Grant wrote in his 1885 memoirs. “At Cold Harbor no advantage whatever was gained to compensate for the heavy loss we sustained.”

This meaning applies well to what we argue is happening within TWC and the MAHA movement more generally. The health freedom movement that was spawned by perceived COVID-19 pandemic tyranny was too dangerous for those in power to attack head on, so instead of expending resources in a futile attempt to do so, they learned from Grant’s mistake. They not only purposely created a kind of cold harbor as a refuge without nourishment, but also as a means to isolate and neutralize those dangerous elements of our society at large that threatened the whole. Instead of throwing all their strength against that impenetrable stronghold, they expend just enough resources to keep dissidents in that harbor, rather than trying to defeat them there.

America emerged from COVID with a wound that no official means could close. Millions had lost confidence not only in particular vaccines, drugs, or public-health officials, but in medicine, government, media, and expertise themselves. What would it mean to manage that injury without allowing it to infect the whole society. without curing it—to acknowledge the betrayal, supply heroes and villains, sell the public its forbidden treatments, celebrate a succession of apparent victories, and give the injured population a separate channel in which to experience its resistance while the deeper machinery they fought against simply continued?

A “free” market acting within designed constraints can discover and amplify useful opposition just as readily as an agency can recruit it, or sincere dissidents can literally be selected, financed, promoted, and made dependent on an ecosystem without ever being ordered to lie. A movement can win its arguments over which products medicine should sell while leaving untouched the more dangerous question of what medicine and health and disease actually are.

The thread we will pull to unravel this entire tapestry, from TWC, to MAHA, to Moderna, to the mRNA platform and beyond, is the recently published, widely lauded and reviled, TWC ivermectin-cancer study which we dissect in the article below.

Westchester County announced details for REV FEST 250, a free, two-day outdoor festival commemorating the 250th anniversary of the American Revolution, to be held Saturday to Sunday October 24 - 25 from 10:00 am – 5:00 pm at Ward Pound Ridge Reservation in Cross River, NY.

As Westchester County’s signature commemoration event, REV FEST 250 brings the American Revolution to life through the stories of patriots, loyalists, and those caught in between, offering a deeper understanding of the people, choices, and conflicts that shaped the birth of a nation. Explore authentic Continental and British Army encampments, meet over 500 volunteer living history exhibitors portraying soldiers and civilians, witness military drills, musket and artillery firing, artisan trades, and hands-on living history that reveals what life was like during the Revolution.

Enjoy live entertainment, browse exhibitors, sample local food trucks, and watch both armies assemble and march toward the weekend's signature attraction—the Reenactment of the Battle of White Plains, a large-scale tactical demonstration featuring over 1,000 reenactors representing 75 different historical uniformed units. With more than two miles of immersive experiences spanning the scenic grounds of Ward Pound Ridge Reservation, there's something to discover around every corner. From historic camps and artisan villages to musical performances and interactive activities, REV FEST 250 offers an unforgettable weekend for families, history enthusiasts, and curious minds of all ages.

Westchester County Executive Ken Jenkins said: “We’re proud to welcome visitors and residents to experience the living legacy of Westchester’s pivotal role in America’s founding. This momentous event commemorates the 250th anniversary of the Battle of White Plains marking the October 28, 1776 clash between General George Washington and British/Hessian forces.  REV FEST 250 is an immersive large-scale festival that’s great fun for the whole family, connecting our County’s roots to the modern day, showcasing how Westchester is a place where history lives on.”

Hi folks,

First, I want to say something to those of you who follow me, something I probably don't say nearly enough.

Thank you. I see you, and I appreciate you.

Sometimes posting here feels like trying to sink a battleship with a BB gun. You put something out there, hoping it might make a difference, knowing full well that most of what you say will disappear into the noise.

I do it not because I expect to change the world with a social media post, but because I hope that somewhere, someone might read something that confirms what they've been sensing, challenges something they've believed, or helps them see something they couldn't see before. If even one person benefits, it's worth the effort.

And to those of you who take the time to read, engage, and share what I write, please know that I genuinely appreciate you.

Now, there's something else on my heart that I want to share. We are living in extraordinarily serious times.

The revelations being brought forward by people like @DataRepublican, whose diligence and work I deeply appreciate, raise troubling questions about what may be happening behind the scenes in our government and political institutions. I want you to understand something about how I've been responding to all of this.

I've been praying. Fervently. Persistently. Specifically.
I've been asking Almighty God to expose the things that are hidden in darkness. Not merely to one political party or another, but to ALL Americans; because here's something I believe with every fiber of my being:

There is nothing hidden from God: Not a conversation. Not a secret meeting. Not a carefully concealed motive. Not a scheme devised behind closed doors.

Nothing.

He sees what we cannot see. He knows what we cannot know. And that is precisely why prayer is so critically important, especially now. Prayer is not wishful thinking. It isn't throwing words into the atmosphere and hoping something good happens.

Prayer is an appeal to the living God, who hears us, who knows the end from the beginning, and whose power is not limited by human institutions, political influence, or earthly authority. And yes, I am praying and trusting God for mercy upon this nation in the coming midterm elections.  I need to make something very clear.

My prayer is not for the destruction of people. It is for the destruction of deception. When I speak about the forces threatening our nation, I am not suggesting that every Democrat, or every person who disagrees with me politically, is evil.

They're human beings. Just like you and me.

I believe some people knowingly participate in wrongdoing. Others may sincerely believe they're doing what is right, even when I believe they've been terribly deceived. And here's why that matters to me personally:

I was once blind, too.

There was a time when I couldn't see what I now believe God has allowed me to see. And if God, in His extraordinary mercy, could open my eyes, who am I to believe He cannot open theirs? So I don't pray for their destruction; I pray for their awakening.

I pray that the deception would be broken. That truth would become unmistakable. That hardened hearts would be softened. That those who have been led astray would recognize it before it's too late.

Because ultimately, I don't want to win an argument against these people. I want them to come to know the God who changed my life.

I believe we're headed into some very turbulent times.
I don't know exactly what lies ahead, and I won't pretend that I do. But I believe the spiritual battle for the direction of this nation is very real, and while voting, speaking out, and holding our elected officials accountable are critically important, I believe there is something even more important.

We need to pray.

Not as a last resort when every political strategy has failed, but as our first response.

Scripture tells us:

"For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this age, against spiritual hosts of wickedness in the heavenly places." — Ephesians 6:12

Our ultimate battle is not against flesh and blood;
that's why we must never allow our political convictions to turn into hatred for the very people Christ came to save. We can stand firmly against what we believe is evil while still praying earnestly for the people caught up in it.

And if you don't know how to pray for our nation, let me share with you something very close to how I pray.

You don't need eloquent words. You don't need a theological degree. You don't need to impress God with your vocabulary. Prayer is simply talking to your Heavenly Father.

He isn't impressed by the number of words we speak, but the posture of our heart.

So this is my prayer:

"Heavenly Father,

I come before You today to petition You for the life of our nation. Father, You see what we cannot see. You know the things that are spoken in secret, the intentions of men's hearts, and the plans that are being made even now; nothing is hidden from You.

And so I ask You, Almighty God, to bring into the light everything that has been concealed in darkness.

Expose corruption wherever it exists. Reveal deception wherever it has taken root. Frustrate every scheme that would bring destruction upon this nation and its people.

Father, I ask that You would awaken Your people.

Stir their hearts. Convict them of their responsibility. Raise up men and women who will stand courageously for truth, righteousness, and justice. Move upon their hearts to participate in the coming elections. Let them not be overcome by apathy, fear, or discouragement.

Awaken Your people, Father, like a mighty army, not to wage war against their fellow man, but to stand against the darkness that seeks to consume us and to always speak truth in the midst of the darkness.  Give them courage to do that, Father.

And Father, I pray especially for those who do not yet know You, as I was once among them.

I remember what it was like to be blind to the truth of who You are. And I remember the mercy You showed me when You opened my eyes; would You do the same for them, Father?

Break through the deception. Remove the spiritual blindness. Soften the hardened hearts.

Let them see that You are not their enemy, but the very One who loves them and desires to save them.

Show them that everything this world has to offer, its wealth, its power, its pleasures, its promises- cannot begin to compare with the surpassing treasure of knowing You.

Father, I pray for our president and those who serve in his administration. Give them wisdom beyond their own understanding. Grant them discernment to recognize dangers before they unfold, courage to do what is right, and humility to seek Your guidance.

Surround them with wise and righteous counsel. Protect them from deception, corruption, and the temptations of power. Where they are wrong, Father, correct them. Where they are weak, strengthen them. Where they lack understanding, grant them wisdom.

I pray for the protection of the innocent, especially the unborn, who have no voice with which to defend themselves, and Father, as there are those who seek to abort the lives of the unborn, I ask You to abort every wicked plan that threatens the life and future of this nation.

Let truth prevail over lies. Let justice prevail over corruption. Let mercy triumph over judgment.

And above all, Father, let Your will be done, because You alone know the end from the beginning. You alone see the whole picture. And You alone are worthy of our complete trust. We do not place our ultimate hope in presidents, political parties, elections, or governments.

Our hope is in You.

Have mercy upon America, Father.

And if it be Your will, grant us another opportunity to turn our hearts toward You.

In the mighty name of Jesus Christ, I ask these things.

Amen."

Friends, I'll leave you with this.

Don't underestimate the power of your prayers. Don't allow the darkness around you to extinguish the light within you. And don't become so consumed with defeating your political opponents that you forget to pray for their souls.

Vote. Speak the truth. Stand for what is right. Refuse to surrender your convictions, but above all, pray.

Because the greatest victory we could ever witness would not simply be the defeat of a political movement, It would be a nation awakening to the God it has forgotten.

God bless you all, and God have mercy upon the United States of America.
