text:
The best deals aren't competitive.

That's the view of my friend and early-stage investor, @alexrubalcava. We talked on @InvestNStartups about VC groupthink, the evolution of moats, embracing technical risk, only investing in greenfield markets, and more. 

Technology risk creates opportunity. Many VCs avoid technically difficult startups, leaving room for investors able to assess and underwrite those risks. As AI makes software easier to build, Alex sees more potential in frontier tech and physical-world applications.

AI is redefining software moats. Faster development weakens traditional defensibility. Alex favors software in regulated or high-stakes settings where accuracy, auditability, accountability, and human oversight still matter.

Sales and product judgment matter more. Alex evaluates founders on whether they can ship, sell, and hire. With building easier, sales velocity and deciding what to build—and when—have become more important.

Venture suffers from groupthink. His public-markets background shapes a contrarian approach grounded in valuation discipline, independent judgment, and finding opportunities overlooked by consensus-driven investors.

Small funds can deliver big returns. Exceptional LP outcomes don't require trillion-dollar exits or mega-funds. An overlooked multibillion-dollar exit can be transformative for a smaller venture fund.

Capital efficiency reduces funding risk. Long runways give startups time to prove their case, especially when follow-on investors favor AI narratives. Alex cites profitable, fast-growing non-AI companies struggling to raise despite strong fundamentals.

Greenfield markets offer an edge. Alex prefers startups serving needs no existing technology addresses over crowded VC-backed categories. Shipping products, winning early customers, and showing demand turn unknown markets into investable opportunities.

Investing expertise must evolve. Alex highlights secondary share sales as a path to LP liquidity, Amplify's founder network as a diligence resource, and the importance of steadily expanding ones circle of competence.

Persistence needs experimentation. Productive founders test new products and sales tactics rather than repeating failed approaches. Alex recalls a founder who shut down a struggling startup and returned half its capital instead of grinding on.

Conviction beats allocation. Alex argues the best opportunities may have just one term sheet. At Stage VP, 42 of his 45 investments were noncompetitive, showing how leading overlooked rounds can create an edge.

Alex is very talented and a great investor. I hope you enjoy this one!

Code 9: The "No-Rush Shipping" Split. Turning a short delivery delay into stacked digital rewards at checkout.

She said Prime members obsess so much over next-day shipping that they leave free checkout rewards on the table every single month.

"Amazon's biggest operational expense is overnight and two-day air freight. When you order something on a Tuesday that you don't actually need until the weekend, Amazon wants to keep that box off an airplane and put it on a cheaper ground truck."

"At checkout, right below the fast Prime delivery option, Amazon frequently offers 'Free No-Rush Shipping,' giving you an instant discount or a promotional digital reward if you let the package arrive a few days later."

"Here is the trick to maximizing it: never bundle four non-urgent items into a single checkout cart when No-Rush rewards are active. The No-Rush reward is triggered per checkout order, not per individual item inside the cart. If you have four household items you don't need until next week, checking them out as four separate orders takes 60 seconds and lets you claim the No-Rush promotional reward four separate times."

"Those digital credits stack up in your account balance and pay for Prime Video movie rentals, Kindle eBooks, digital music, or app purchases without touching your credit card."

"She said splitting non-urgent carts is the easiest passive reward on the platform. 'If you are ordering toothpaste, trash bags, and phone cables that you won't open until next week anyway, why bundle them into one reward? Split the checkouts, click No-Rush on each one, and collect multiple digital credits just for letting Amazon use a ground truck.'"

If you open customer chat and simply ask for a 'price match,' the bot and the support rep will recite the standard policy: 'Amazon does not offer post-purchase price adjustments.'"

"Most people accept that answer and lose the $40. They forget that free Prime returns give the buyer leverage over Amazon's shipping math."

"When an item drops significantly in price while you are still inside your 30-day free return window, open customer chat and avoid the phrase 'price match.' Instead, lay out the simple logistics math: 'This item just dropped by $40 on the product page. Since I am in my free return window, I can order a new one today at $110 and send my current unit back via UPS for free, which costs Amazon two shipping labels and restocking labor. Would you rather issue a $40 courtesy credit on my current order to save us both the return shipment?'"

"While they aren't required to match prices, live support reps have discretionary promotional credit allowances to resolve customer friction and prevent pointless round-trip shipments."

"She said framing it around the cost of a free return changes the outcome. 'If you ask for a policy price match, their workflow tells them to say no. When you politely point out that you are about to trigger a free UPS return and rebuy the exact same item from their warehouse today, many agents will offer a courtesy credit or partial refund on the spot because it makes total sense for both sides.'"

text:
Code 2: The "LPN" Barcode Sticker. The warehouse License Plate Number that gives you instant leverage when a "New" item isn't new.

She said this three-letter code is printed on a small white sticker on millions of packages, and knowing what it means gives you immediate leverage with customer support.

"Every single item that passes through an Amazon return center gets slapped with a white barcode sticker starting with the letters 'LPN,' which stands for License Plate Number. That sticker ties the physical box to a specific return ID in Amazon's internal database, recording the return history of that exact unit."

"Here is why you need to check every box you order: fulfillment center workers move fast under intense hourly quotas. Mistakes happen constantly. A returned item with an LPN sticker occasionally gets routed back into the 'New' inventory bin by mistake."

"If you pay full retail price for a 'New' item and it arrives with a white LPN barcode sticker stuck over the original manufacturer barcode, you did not receive untouched factory inventory. You paid full price for a previously returned unit."

"When this happens, you don't have to pack it up and drive to UPS. Open the Amazon customer chat and use the exact warehouse terminology. Tell the agent: 'I paid full retail price for a New item, but the package arrived with an LPN return sticker on the box. Since I received previously returned inventory, I would like an open-box partial credit adjustment to keep it instead of returning it.'"

"She said mentioning the LPN code changes the chat conversation immediately. 'The moment you point out the LPN sticker, the support rep knows a fulfillment grading error happened. Because it costs Amazon money to ship that item back and re-grade it, support agents can offer a partial refund or promotional credit on the spot so you keep the item without triggering a return.'"

text:
Hiring Brand & Communications Lead

About the job

Rackan Technologies is a Lagos-based fintech building cross-border payments that help individuals and businesses move money between Africa and the rest of the world. Its promise is simple: money that goes further, with seamless payments and borderless possibilities.

Rackan operates a Nigerian entity and a registered money services business (MSB) in Canada. Today it serves businesses moving value out of Nigeria at scale, and it is launching products for both consumers and businesses:

For individuals: a remittance app that makes sending money home from the UK, US and Canada to Nigeria, Ghana and Kenya fast, reliable and fairly priced.

For businesses: multi-currency accounts to collect, hold and pay out in local currencies, major foreign currencies and stablecoins, so African businesses can pay suppliers and get paid globally.
Rackan is a small, ambitious team. The person in this role will shape how Africa and the world see Rackan.

Role Summary

Rackan is hiring its first Brand & Communications Lead to build the function from the ground up and grow into Head of Brand & Communications.

Title

Brand & Communications Lead (Senior Associate)

Company

Rackan Technologies

Location

Lagos, Nigeria (hybrid)

Reports to

Co-founder / Executive leadership

Type

Full-time

Growth path

Head of Brand & Communications, owning brand, marketing, PR, events and internal communications

Responsibilities

The successful candidate will own how Rackan looks, sounds and is talked about, across customers, partners, regulators, media and the internal team.

Brand strategy and identity

Define and protect Rackan's positioning, voice and visual identity across the company and both product lines.

Build and enforce brand guidelines for everything Rackan publishes, from app copy to event booths.

Track brand health: awareness, sentiment and share of voice in Rackan's markets.

Communications and PR

Build relationships with tech, business and financial media across Africa, the UK and North America.

Write and place press releases, op-eds, founder interviews and announcements for launches, partnerships and milestones.

Own executive visibility: speaking slots, panels, podcasts and thought leadership for Rackan's founders and leaders.

Crisis, reputation and stakeholder communications

Set up issues and crisis communications playbooks for incidents such as payout delays, outages, fraud or regulatory questions.

Monitor social and traditional media daily and respond quickly and calmly.

Support clear, compliant communications with regulators, banking partners and investors, working with Legal and Compliance.

Content and storytelling

Run Rackan's content engine across LinkedIn, X, Instagram, the website, newsletters and video.

Tell customer, partner and team stories that build trust in cross-border money movement.

Events and partnerships

Plan Rackan's presence at industry events (for example Money20/20, GTR Africa and Moonshot by TechCabal), including sponsorships, booths and speaking.

Manage co-marketing with partners and the wider ecosystem.

Internal communications

Keep the team aligned on company news, wins and culture as Rackan grows.
Marketing collaboration
Work with Product and Growth on launch campaigns, so brand and performance marketing tell one story.

Expectations: building the team

This is not joining a team; it is building one. Within 12 months, Rackan expects a working Brand & Communications function with clear processes, a small team and visible results.

First 30 days: learn and audit

Learn Rackan's products, customers, markets and regulatory context.
Audit Rackan's current brand, channels, media coverage and competitor positioning.
Present findings and quick wins to leadership.

By 90 days: foundations

Ship a brand and communications strategy for the next 12 months, with goals and a budget.
Finalise brand guidelines, messaging and tone of voice for both product lines.
Set up a content calendar, media list and approval workflow with Product, Legal and Compliance.

Put a crisis communications playbook in place before the consumer launch.

By 6 months: momentum
Lead launch communications for the consumer and business products.

Land consistent coverage in top-tier African tech and business media, plus at least one international outlet.

Secure regular speaking and event opportunities for leadership.
Define the team structure and make the first hire (for example, a content and social specialist).

By 12 months: a function, not a person

Run a small team with clear roles, targets, and agency or freelance partners where useful.

Report quarterly on brand health, share of voice, coverage and content performance.

Make Rackan a name people in African fintech recognise and trust.

Strong performance in this role leads to Head of Brand & Communications, with marketing, PR, events and internal communications reporting into it.

Requirements

4–6 years of brand, communications or PR experience, with at least 2 of those years in fintech, tech or financial services.

Must have

4–6 years in brand management, corporate communications, PR or brand storytelling, in-house or at an agency.

At least 2 years in fintech, technology, banking or another regulated industry.

A portfolio of campaigns, launches or media coverage led end to end.
Excellent written English: press releases, op-eds, social copy and executive talking points.
Working relationships with tech and business journalists in Nigeria or across Africa.

Experience handling a sensitive issue or crisis in public.

Comfort working alone at first: setting priorities, building processes and delivering without a big team.
A degree in Communications, Mass Communication, Journalism, Marketing, English or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Nice to have
Experience with cross-border payments, remittance or B2B fintech.

Exposure to UK, North American or pan-African audiences.

Event planning or sponsorship management at industry conferences.
Experience hiring or managing a small team, agencies or freelancers.
Basic design and video skills (Canva, Figma, CapCut or similar).
Professional membership, such as NIPR or CIPR.

What's On Offer

A rare chance to build a brand and communications function from day one, with a clear path to Head of Brand & Communications.
Direct access to founders and leadership, and a real say in how Rackan shows up.
Competitive pay, with details shared during the process.

Exposure to cross-border fintech across Africa, the UK and North America.

How To Apply Or Recommend Someone

Send a CV, a short note on why this role, and 2–3 work samples (a campaign, a press placement or a piece of writing) to careers@librastratconsulting.com, copying peopleops@rackantech.com.

text:
Unitree launches H2-X Kung Fu Legend Guardian

Unitree, known for its cutting-edge robotics, has just unveiled their latest creation: the H2-X Kung Fu Legend Guardian. This isn’t your average robotic assistant; it's designed to be a personal bodyguard capable of performing martial arts moves and lifting cars by hand.
What’s the Big Deal?

Unitree’s new robot is making waves in the robotics industry, not just because of its impressive physical capabilities but also due to its potential as a security solution. The H2-X Guardian boasts an 8-hour battery life, which is a significant improvement over previous models that typically lasted around three hours. This extended runtime makes it more practical for real-world use.
How Does It Work?

The H2-X Guardian features 71 degrees of freedom (DOF), allowing it to mimic human movement with remarkable flexibility. Its advanced gripping capabilities enable it to perform tasks like lifting heavy objects and executing precise martial arts moves, such as kicking dents into car doors. This level of physical prowess is what sets the H2-X apart from other robotic assistants.
Why Should You Care?

The introduction of a robot that can physically defend its owner raises several important questions about the future of personal security. While the idea of having a robotic bodyguard sounds like something out of a movie, it’s becoming increasingly plausible with advancements in robotics technology. However, this shift also brings ethical and practical concerns to the forefront.
The Ethical Quandary

The H2-X Guardian is marketed as a protector, but its capabilities could easily be repurposed for more nefarious uses. Imagine a scenario where one person hires a robot to protect them from perceived threats, only to have another individual use a similar robot to intimidate or coerce others into compliance. The line between protection and coercion becomes blurred in this context.
Practical Limitations

While the H2-X Guardian is impressive on paper, there are practical limitations to consider. For instance, its ability to perform martial arts moves might be more show than substance. Can it really fend off multiple attackers effectively? Moreover, the cost of such a robot remains prohibitive for most individuals, limiting its accessibility.
What’s Next?

The release of the H2-X Guardian signals a new era in robotics—one where machines are not just tools but active participants in our personal lives and security protocols. As these technologies advance, we’ll need to grapple with questions about their ethical use and regulation. So what changes for you? If you’re considering investing in such technology, it’s crucial to weigh the benefits against potential risks.
The Fine Print

While Unitree’s H2-X Guardian offers an exciting glimpse into the future of robotics, there are several caveats to consider. For one, the cost of such advanced technology remains high, making it inaccessible for most people. Additionally, the ethical implications of having a robot that can physically defend its owner need careful consideration.
Cost and Accessibility

The H2-X Guardian is priced at 95,000 yuan (approximately $13,600 USD), which places it out of reach for many individuals. This high cost means that only those with significant financial resources will be able to benefit from its capabilities, raising questions about equity in access to advanced technology.
Regulatory Challenges

As robotic bodyguards become more common, regulatory bodies will need to address the ethical and legal implications of their use. Questions around liability, privacy, and the potential for misuse will require clear guidelines and regulations to ensure responsible deployment.
Ethical Use Cases

While the H2-X Guardian is marketed as a personal security solution, its capabilities could be used in various other contexts. For instance, it might find applications in law enforcement or military scenarios where physical protection is necessary. However, these uses also raise ethical concerns about the potential for abuse and misuse.
Future Developments

Unitree’s H2-X Guardian represents just one step in a broader trend towards more advanced robotics technology. As companies continue to innovate, we can expect to see further developments in areas like AI integration, improved battery life, and enhanced physical capabilities.
Community Feedback

The announcement of the H2-X Guardian has sparked discussions among tech enthusiasts and industry experts alike. Many are excited about the potential benefits, while others raise concerns about ethical implications and practical limitations.

So what do you think? Is a robotic bodyguard something that excites or worries you? Let’s discuss this in the comments below!

text:
Your stocks do not necessarily have to sit idle in your portfolio.

Yesterday, I shared my thoughts on the Q3 earnings reports from $TSLA and $META, particularly what I wanted to see from Tesla's automotive margins and Meta's massive spending on AI infrastructure.

With both companies reporting after the US market closes, there is another part of stock trading that I wanted to discuss, especially for investors who already have a significant amount of their capital tied up in long-term stock positions.

You might already be comfortable with your existing positions, but that does not necessarily mean you want to sell part of your portfolio every time another trading opportunity comes along.

Traditional brokers such as Robinhood, Moomoo, and Interactive Brokers already offer ways to borrow against eligible securities or use portfolio margin, so this isn't entirely a new concept.

The difference with @Bitget is that its rToken ecosystem brings eligible tokenized stock holdings into the same trading environment as crypto, letting supported assets serve multiple purposes without requiring you to sell them first.

For example, instead of simply holding rTSLA or rMETA in your spot account, eligible rTokens can also contribute margin toward supported futures positions through Bitget's Unified Trading Account (UTA).

Someone holding stock tokens can use their collateral value to support another position while maintaining their original stock-linked exposure, though the actual margin contribution depends on the asset's collateral discount rate and the account's available margin.

Notably, Bitget also lets users use selected rTokens as collateral for crypto loans, borrowing assets such as USDT against eligible holdings.

Now, having that kind of flexibility does not mean I would automatically use my entire stock portfolio as collateral. If Tesla drops for example, the value of rTSLA used as collateral could also decline, and if there is already an open leveraged position moving against you, the combination could quickly put additional pressure on your account.

Borrowing also involves interest costs, while futures margin comes with liquidation risks, so using the same holdings across multiple financial products should not be mistaken for getting additional capital without consequences.

For those wondering how the margin feature works, Bitget requires users to enable its Unified Trading Account and switch to Advanced mode, where eligible rTokens can contribute toward margin requirements for supported positions.

There are also differences between cross margin and isolated margin, so I would suggest understanding how each mode handles collateral and liquidation before using either one.

You can find the official explanation here: https://t.co/cidtdOcZCX

And for those looking into borrowing against their stock tokens rather than using them directly as trading margin, this guide explains the collateral requirements and how the crypto loan process works: https://t.co/INl9H6cPyE

Moving on to the next topic, I have already discussed Bitget's rToken transfer service in my previous posts on how stockholders can move their existing holdings from traditional brokers into Bitget.

But beyond the process itself, I think the next thing worth discussing is what investors can actually do with those assets once they arrive, now that some rTokens can be used for futures margin or as collateral for supported crypto loans.

For someone already managing stocks and crypto across multiple platforms, having those options within the same ecosystem could make capital allocation more flexible, provided they understand the added risks.

The exchange is also running an ongoing transfer campaign that offers at least 200 USDT worth of rSPCX for an eligible first transfer of $5,000 or more, with higher reward tiers for larger transfers.

Those rewards are distributed in installments and users need to meet the applicable holding requirements to receive subsequent distributions.

The campaign runs until November 18, and the supported stocks, transfer process, and reward conditions can be found here: https://t.co/e7rOBFACsi

Overall, holding a stock long term and using its value to support another trading activity are two different decisions, and more options can help investors who understand the risks involved.

But I would still be careful about tying several positions to the same pool of collateral, because an earnings-heavy week like this could affect the margin available for another.

There is a fine line between making better use of your capital and exposing that same capital to more risk, and understanding that distinction matters more than simply having access to additional leverage.

text:
I was late for my tour. I had scheduled a tour, too, earlier in the day, with this company “The Amish Experience” which parasitically allows you access into a bunch of Amish people’s houses for an Authentic Amish Home Visit Experience. I paid ~$60 for the “Amish Meal” Experience, where they take you on a little tour of the town and then you go into a Amish Family’s house for supper and they feed you. It’s limited to 14 bodies max, and they seem to fill about half the spots each time. I was late, for this, and their bus leaves at 4:30 sharp, so I said “Uh can I just get the 5 o clock instead.” and the three or four white people in the lobby of this tour agency were overjoyed, they had the same idea. The 5 o clock is a slightly different program, no meal but a lot of the same kind of stuff, three hours long, and so I just joined for that.

Before the tour I took more drugs, for some reason. I was almost late AGAIN, fishing through the back of my van for a little tin containing psilocybin gummies I bought legally in San Francisco back in… March. I go through drugs slowly. I hesitated a bit, before taking these: I have a theory that psychedelics (shrooms, acid, DMT) kick you out of whatever ‘road’ you’re on mentally, and put you on a different path. Which can be helpful or harmful depending on your current trajectory, state. I took a heavy dose of psychs in Summer of 2024, immediately became Worst Boyfriend Ever, which I’m still counting as an extremely positive development, and did not re-up in any way until Spring of ’26, after failing to ship the second book. More like, failing to conjure the guts to press ‘publish’ on the thing I had just spent three weeks of life crafting, for reasons I won’t get into now. That, coupled with a little influence from Tao Lin, drove me to take psychs again in the Spring ’26 for the first time since Summer ’24, which made for my longest abstinence from that class of drugs since I first tried them at age 18, in 2017. Don’t mind me, just trying to draw connections here between my actions, attitudes, psychology, and chemical intake.

At 4:59 I stepped up to the door of the van with my mouth half-full of sticky bun. The Old Man who ran the tour, Chris, greeted me with a stale mix of warmth and disdain. “We almost left without ye. Got your ticket?” I dug into my pocket for the little pink piece of paper he watched me get 12 minutes ago. He let me onto the tour bus which was filled with four other people, all women. Again I can’t tell if this is real or just in my head, but the vibe of every space seems to drop down into hell as soon as I enter the room. It was an older lady, a strongfat cornfed blonde mom in her late 30s, and her two skinny pre-teen daughters. And me. 27 year old man. I just said Hi and sat directly behind the Mom.
The bus took off, the tour began. I didn’t take my phone. Chris, also very old, I would later learn 79 but still wily and sharp as anybody, said many times do not take pictures of the Amish. Please do not take pictures, the tour will end if you take pictures, they will ask us to leave. It’s okay if you take pictures of the animals, or the landscape, but as for the people—like this lady rolling by on her scooter here, they do not take kindly to being photographed, they think it erodes the soul. I completely understood. Fuck my blog, the internet isn’t real right now, I don’t need pictures. I’ll just try to be in person and see and remember, for once.

Here was the lowlight of my tour: This little girl, "Barbie," age 11, rubbed her arm nervously as I tried to explain my 'blog' on the 'internet' to her Amish father. We were in the back of their barn, surrounded by shitting cows.

Female intuition is real, she could tell I'm a predator creep who's full of shit, all the Amish can I think, which makes it very difficult for me to be around them. And I wasn't planning on explaining myself like this, I just wanted to observe them like zoo animals, but this tour was a little more personal than that, so in each of the 3  houses I visited the tour guide made me explain, over and over, Who I Am and What I'm Doing here in Lancaster County.

I can barely explain myself to baristas at Starbucks. Every family got a different story. This fat swarthy blonde on the tour with her own two pre-teen daughters clocked me instantly: are you a journalist? I just laughed. Kind of, yeah. I left out the whole "fucking girls in my van" aspect of it and just said that I travel a lot, I'm on a long road trip from Seattle to NYC. The tour guide had nothing but shit to say about NYC. All the rudest, most-ill adjusted customers come from New York City, or California. I tried to deflect the conversations away from Me and What I'm Up To but they just wouldn't stop. One woman asked for the name of my book and I just sighed... it's called "Worst Boyfriend Ever." Her two daughters laughed covering their mouths. I knew nobody would look it up after, most people don't and these people were especially offline. The other adult women on this tour seemed to be more interested in the Amish farming techniques than the people. I was high and on shrooms so I just stood stunned through most of it trying not to seem like a pedophile.

Barbie gave us a tour of her family's milking operation. The kids grow up quick when their brains aren't fucked by screens. The cows looked sad and stared at me begging for help. I wondered if I was the only one who could see it.

All these people have 8 kids and 40 grandkids. It's a nightmare trying to decide where to eat on the holidays. They make these totally arbitrary decisions about what Is and Is Not Allowed, no gas no electricity so they use air power for things like elevators in their homes, solar panels on every Amish roof. They're not secluded from the rest of the world here in Lancaster, they just play every game with a handicap. While driving my big heavy van with bad brakes and no insurance I am frequently acquainted with these stoic farm people wearing straw hats sitting in buggy-carriages pulled by horses waiting at intersections trying to Merge. The late-teens women are scarcely seen. On the bus I learned that "scooters are allowed... but not bicycles. it would let them get too far from home."

I deflected questions about myself all night. We were all sitting in this old widow's living room, every person dead sober except for me, as they tried to understand why I would voluntarily sleep in my van, for so long, unmarried, childless, "writing..." one of the Amish guys was sure I said "riding." It's like, fiction, I have a book, you don't understand.. The old widow offered me some delicious apple cider. They put two types of apples, and pears in it. It was thick and I had several cups. Her name was Sarah and we were instructed not to sit in that green rocking chair in the corner of the room, because that's where Ike used to sit, before he recently died. Sarah looked like Benjamin Franklin if he were a woman. Every time I said "my phone" or "online" every person in the room cringed. I'm sorry, I just can't explain my life without it. That's how I find places to eat, that's how I get money, that's how I found this. I couldn't think of the right questions to ask, I didn't want to get "too philosophical" and start dissecting these peoples' brains, prompting them to question their way of life. My own sense of reality feels increasingly fragile lately and I know philosophy is a dead end.

The old widow asked for the name of my book again, as we left. I just shook my head and smiled knowing there is no universe in which this thing actually reaches her. Worst Boyfriend Ever will never be in bookstores, and she will never use the internet. Still I yelled it out, as if warning her it would be hitting the shelves at her local library next week.

The bus got back to the parking lot and the tour ended and I scurried out of there as quickly as I could, before anybody could ask any more questions. I drove to the only pub open in town and ate a steak salad alone. I thought about those Amish people we pay to interrogate like zoo animals and how sick they must be of that treatment. Explaining themselves over and over. I hoped they were getting paid well. I wondered if there were any whorehouses in this town. I thought it might be funny if, when I got to New York, I did another show, ticketed, called "Live Rapist Q&A -- Ask Me Anything!" Could be funny.

There is one of these entries for every day of the past few months. They are all here: https://t.co/6GRlJ1yfsf

Suspected source
Evidence points to https://t.co/sIVPOJz0tY (Louisiana/New Orleans-based), a widely used ID-scanning and verification vendor whose clients have included Hertz, Target, FedEx, Caesars, and large cannabis retailers. The company processes tens of millions of verifications per month. https://t.co/sIVPOJz0tY has said it is investigating a potential security incident, has engaged forensics and counsel, and is coordinating with law enforcement; it has not yet confirmed the full scope.
High-profile and researcher confirmations
Krebs’s own Virginia license was offered as a free sample. Other researchers and members of the public whose licenses appeared have matched the scan timestamps to their own travel or purchases. Records for U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and at least one FBI assistant director were also visible in the dataset.
The FBI’s New Orleans field office opened an official inquiry. Krebs and other security researchers have called it one of the more damaging ID-document exposures they have seen because of the photos plus the breadth of everyday places that scan licenses.
Practical takeaway: If you have rented a car, stayed in certain hotels, bought alcohol/cannabis in a regulated market, or otherwise had your physical ID scanned in recent years, there is a realistic chance your license image is in this set. Monitor credit, watch for account-takeover attempts, and treat any unexpected “ID verification” requests with extra suspicion. Official notifications from the vendor or affected businesses, if they come, will take time.

text:
Indiana AG Investigator Threatened Prosecution Over a Facebook Post. A Federal Judge Calls It Coercion.

Judge grants request for a preliminary injunction, finding that an investigator likely used his authority to silence protected political speech

INDIANAPOLIS — An investigator with Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita’s office who threatened a private citizen with prosecution over political Facebook posts has been ordered by a federal judge to stop, following a First Amendment lawsuit filed by the ACLU of Indiana.

In an October 20 ruling, U.S. District Judge Sarah Evans Barker granted a preliminary injunction after finding that Kurt Spivey, Director of Investigations for the Attorney General’s office, likely used his authority to pressure Monroe County resident Lee Lawmaster into silence. The court also rejected Spivey’s attempt to dismiss the lawsuit.

In April, Lawmaster posted “86” alongside the names of several elected officials on Facebook, including Rokita, Lieutenant Governor Micah Beckwith, and U.S. Senator Jim Banks. His comments followed the indictment of former FBI Director James Comey over a social media post featuring the phrase “86 47.” Lawmaster used the phrase to express political disagreement and support for the right to criticize public officials.

Two days later, Spivey showed up at Lawmaster’s Bloomington home, displayed his badge, and warned that he had “crossed the line.” Spivey told him, “We could easily indict you over this today,” but offered to “let this one slide” if he toned down his political rhetoric.

Fearing prosecution, Lawmaster stopped commenting on elected officials’ Facebook pages. The ACLU of Indiana filed suit on his behalf on May 7.

The court rejected Spivey’s argument that the encounter was simply a polite conversation about a potential threat. Judge Barker found that Spivey had used his authority to pressure Lawmaster into silence, writing, “That is coercion by any reasonable measure.”

“We're pleased with the court's ruling,” said Ken Falk, Legal Director at the ACLU of Indiana. “Mr. Lawmaster was never charged with a crime, but when a state official shows up on your doorstep and threatens prosecution over something you posted online, the message is pretty clear. The government shouldn't be able to accomplish through intimidation what the First Amendment prohibits it from doing directly.”

The preliminary injunction prohibits Spivey and those acting on his behalf within the Attorney General’s Investigations Division from threatening Lawmaster with legal sanctions intended to suppress or punish his past or future political posts involving “86.”

The lawsuit, Lawmaster v. Spivey, remains ongoing.

**Drone Strikes on a Market in the Disputed Abyei Region Kill at Least 73; South Sudan Summons Sudan's Ambassador**

Drones struck a market north of Abyei town on Monday, killing at least 73 people and wounding 19, caretaker information minister Yohana Akol Ngor told Reuters on Tuesday; he blamed Sudan's armed forces but offered no evidence. Abyei is an oil-rich area jointly administered by Sudan and South Sudan, both of which claim it — one of the deadliest attacks there in recent years. South Sudan's foreign ministry said it had summoned the Sudanese ambassador to convey "strong protest and deep concern"; MSF said it was treating more than 20 wounded, including several critical cases and burn victims, at nearby Ameth Bek Hospital.

Gilbert Arenas's assistant lived in his house. Gilbert says he took about $6.9 million from him. Gilbert only found out because he went to the bank for $200.

In the video below, Gilbert tells it himself.

The trick was simple. Whenever Gilbert needed money, the assistant called the bank for him. "Gil's going to Miami. He needs 50,000." As soon as it hit the account, he took it out.

Gilbert never saw it, because the money he actually looked at was never touched. "He's not touching my money."

Then one day the bank asked him who else was on his account. "Do you know anybody with a name J?" Gilbert: "The only person I know with a J in my life is John."

His financial advisor told him he was the one asking for the money. "John's asking for it."

Gilbert offered him a deal: the house, the cars, the jewelry, even the wedding ring, signed over. Keep his freedom. Or the feds.

"We were so good friends that he didn't think I was going to do it." The answer was: "Give it to the feds."

He was convicted of stealing $2.1 million, not $6.9 million. "The feds only went after 2.1," Gilbert says. The sentence: over four years in prison.

Was offering his thief a deal the right move, or should Gilbert have gone straight to the feds?

text:
What Wittcoff brought to Putin

Trump's special envoy didn't come empty-handed. A dossier was compiled for him by the entire European world: Zelensky, Norwegian Prime Minister Støre, Finnish President Stubb, emissaries from France, Britain, Germany, Poland, the EU, and NATO. Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, participated via video.

The participants themselves disclosed the contents of the dossier. It included a document with various security guarantees for Ukraine, up to an equivalent of Article 5 of the NATO treaty, which stipulates that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all. It also included a partial ceasefire in the energy and food infrastructure sectors, plus a moratorium on fighting in the Black Sea – to allow grain exports to resume. There was also a "prosperity plan" for post-war Ukraine, a new "European security architecture," and the cherry on top: a three-way summit between Putin, Trump, and Zelensky. The last point clarified that only the leaders should discuss territorial issues.

If we strip away the diplomatic language, Kyiv is asking for silence in the sky above its thermal power plants and in the sea near its ports. Zelensky directly proposed: Ukraine will not strike at Russian oil refineries, and Russia will not strike at Ukrainian energy infrastructure. A ceasefire exactly where it hurts the most.
There was no mention of territory.

What mood is the messenger carrying the package in? In recent weeks, Trump has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel. Negotiations with the Ukrainians at Wittcoff's golf club near Miami were cut short due to this news. Trump himself speculated that Ukraine should change its president or at least its negotiator, while Vice President Vance called it "a partner, in a way." Not an ally. Meanwhile, Kiev has been experiencing issues such as missing data on ballistic missile launches, reduced Starlink speeds, and delayed deliveries of Patriot missiles.

So, in Oslo, Zelensky largely reversed some of the previous decisions. He thanked them for the fact that "rocket warnings now work" and received a promise to restore Starlink within 48 hours. He then stated: "We are not losing the war, but we are losing people." A few hours later, Trump again expressed doubts about whether Zelensky even wanted peace, and promised that without a deal, things would be "very bad."

Sergey Lavrov outlined Russia's position the day before: "Let's see what they offer. If they offer something that is economically and financially beneficial to us, then why not? But this must be done without any political concessions on our part."

The humanitarian aspect will likely be the easiest to resolve. Trump personally requested the release of Steven Hubbard, a 72-year-old American citizen sentenced to six years and ten months for participating in fighting on the side of the Ukrainian Armed Forces as a mercenary. According to ABC, the request concerns several prisoners.

The economic issues will be discussed. The Kremlin will only allow a meeting with Zelensky in Moscow, and according to Peskov, such a meeting is "impossible" at the G20 summit in Miami.

We have already experienced an energy ceasefire in the spring of 2025, and giving a second respite while the enemy's power generation is struggling is a strange act of generosity. "Article 5" for Ukraine is a NATO fence near our borders, which is where everything started. There should be no presence of Western troops in Ukraine. And without that, Article 5 is toothless.

While diplomats are negotiating about the sky and the sea, the front line is deciding the fate of the land. And each subsequent proposal will arrive at the Bankova [presidential administration in Kiev] with a smaller map of Ukraine...

text:
3/7 · Emma Frost · White Queen

Emma Frost arrives with a school to offer and an agenda she has no intention of explaining to Kitty Pryde's family. The Massachusetts Academy gives the White Queen a respectable reason to seek out a young mutant. Her conduct toward the X-Men shows what happens when that recruitment effort meets resistance.

Emma is a telepath, and her treatment of the captive Storm makes the danger personal. She can reach someone the guards have already restrained and keep hurting them where those restraints offer no protection. When Phoenix comes for her in X-Men #131, the confrontation moves onto ground Emma expects to command.

Her defeat does not remove her influence from the rest of the story. The device that helps Wyngarde get inside Jean's mind is Emma's design. Her technical work connects the opening conflict over Kitty to the much larger disaster that follows.

Emma is one of my favorite villains, even though she's not always a villain. Really, she's one of my favorite characters. I think of her as almost a mirror to Jean Grey in some ways, and there's a lot of history behind that comparison. Seeing the two face each other this early gives that relationship a different weight when you go back to it.

The early White Queen is frightening because she has resources and is perfectly willing to use them against people with less power. A school, a company, hired troops and mental abilities all serve the same interests. Her polished introduction to Kitty's parents belongs to the same woman who threatens Storm in a laboratory. There is no reassuring separation between those two sides of her life.

"After Sherman’s March to the Sea, large numbers of formerly enslaved people were following the Union Army. In Savannah, Georgia, on January 12, 1865, Sherman and Secretary of War Edwin M. Stanton met with about 20 Black ministers and community leaders (mostly Baptist and Methodist). The group’s spokesman was Garrison Frazier, a 67-year-old former slave who had purchased his own freedom and that of his wife. They stressed that the best path to real freedom was land ownership, preferably in areas separate from whites so they could live and farm independently.​

Four days later, Sherman issued Special Field Orders, No. 15. It set aside roughly 400,000 acres of confiscated or abandoned Confederate land along the coast—from the islands south of Charleston, South Carolina, through the Sea Islands and abandoned rice fields (extending about 30 miles inland) to the St. Johns River area in Florida. Each family of freed people could claim a plot of no more than 40 acres of tillable ground, with military protection until they could protect themselves or Congress regulated their titles. These were “possessory” titles (temporary occupation rights), not full permanent ownership.​

The order itself did not mention mules. Later, surplus Army mules (and sometimes other animals) were loaned to some of the settlers to help with farming. That is how the full popular phrase “40 acres and a mule” arose.​
Historynet
Implementation moved quickly. Brig. Gen. Rufus Saxton oversaw distribution. By June 1865, an estimated 40,000 freed people had settled on about 400,000 acres of this “Sherman Land.” Titles were issued under the order (and later through the Freedmen’s Bureau). Recent research has identified more than 1,200 specific possessory titles granted in coastal Georgia and South Carolina.​

There were earlier related steps: in 1863 Lincoln had ordered some confiscated South Carolina land sold to freedmen in 20-acre plots, and Treasury Secretary Salmon Chase expanded offerings toward 40 acres per family. But Sherman’s order is the source of the famous phrase and the main concrete wartime effort of this scale.​

What happened afterward
The arrangement was short-lived. After Lincoln’s assassination in April 1865, President Andrew Johnson took a different approach. On May 29, 1865, he issued an amnesty proclamation that allowed most former Confederates to regain their property. He ordered the land restored to the original white owners. By late 1865 (and continuing into 1866–67), the large majority of the freed people were removed from the land. Only a small number who had stronger legal titles kept their holdings; most lost what they had received. Later measures offered limited alternatives (such as warrants to buy smaller plots of government land elsewhere at a low price), but these were far short of the original distribution.​

The episode is widely remembered as an early, limited form of land-based reparations or economic support for the formerly enslaved." Grok Ai

text:
話題になっている

新潟県が、米国の有力メディア『National Geographic（ナショナル ジオグラフィック）』が毎年発表する「Best of the World 2027（2027年に行くべき世界の旅行先25選）」に選出されました

について

全文貼っておきます（一部、リンクがある部分もありますので注意）

（英文）

In Niigata Prefecture, on the west coast of Honshu, scenes like a bullet train speeding through flooded rice fields epitomize Japan’s famous contrast between modernity and tradition.
Daichi Tatsumi
Niigata, Japan

______________________________________________________________________________________

Why go: A peculiar art fest and a centuries-old fermentation tradition offer new ways to explore a quieter corner of Japan

______________________________________________________________________________________

Niigata Prefecture sits in the heart of Japan’s snow country, the central region on the Sea of Japan renowned for legendary snowfall, which draws skiers from around the world. Next year, well before the snow arrives, the world’s largest outdoor art festival takes over some 200 villages across Niigata. The 10th year of the Echigo Tsumari Art Triennale, held from July through November, includes a series of site-specific art installations themed around reuse, which will take over abandoned schools, terraced rice fields, and even tunnels burrowing through mountains, serving as a model for both architectural reuse and rural revitalization. The lineup is still being finalized but will include international heavyweights such as British sculptor Antony Gormley, whose piece will strip the interior of an old timber farmhouse that’s been crushed by years of snowfall, as well as French conceptual artist Annette Messager and Japanese sculptor Tadashi Kawamata.

Niigata’s long, cold winters have helped foster a culture of sake brewing and other kinds of fermentation. The area is also home to dozens of sansai varieties (traditionally foraged wild mountain shoots or vegetables) and some of Japan’s most complex, delicious soy sauces and misos. The tradition takes center stage at the newly opened Hakko House (whose name means “fermentation”) in Nagaoka, where chef Sho Suzuki’s 11-course meal leans into what’s seasonal and foraged: think royal fern shoots and wild asparagus glazed in nanban koji, a spicy fermented paste, or tuna with house-made koji soy sauce. Each course is paired with an exclusive regional sake specifically commissioned by the chef.

Chef Suzuki owns a mini empire of fermented Niigata “snow food” shops and restaurants. Many line Nagaoka’s mile-long Hakko Trip, a self-guided fermentation trail that stops at heritage miso producers, a historic dango shop serving syrupy mochi skewers, and a sake brewery that revives heirloom rice once near extinction before brewing, fermenting, and snow-cooling it in traditional yukimuro, or snow warehouses. The long-practiced Niigata technique allows sake to mature at a low and slow 37°F—and it is a reminder that the slow pace of snow country produces some pretty magical results. —Adam H. Graham

Our destination spotlight explores Niigata’s food culture and more, including its popular ski resorts and some of Japan’s best swimming and snorkeling.

（Gemini訳）

本州の西海岸に位置する新潟県では、水田の中を新幹線が駆け抜ける光景に、近代性と伝統という日本ならではの有名な対比が象徴されています。
Tatsumi Daichi  新潟県

おすすめの理由：一風変わった芸術祭と数世紀にわたる発酵の伝統が、日本の静かな一角を探索する新たな方法を提供してくれます。
新潟県は、世界中からスキーヤーを引き付ける伝説的な降雪で知られる日本海側の中心地域、日本の「雪国」の核心に位置しています。
来年、雪が降り積もるよりもずっと前に、世界最大級の野外芸術祭が新潟県内の約200の集落を舞台に開催されます。7月から11月まで開催される第10回「大地の芸術祭 越後妻有アートトリエンナーレ」では、「再利用」をテーマにしたサイト・スピーシフィック（その土地の文脈に合わせた）なアート作品の数々が登場します。これらは廃校や棚田、さらには山を貫くトンネルなどを舞台とし、建築の再利用および地方創生のモデルとなります。出展ラインナップは現在最終調整中ですが、長年の積雪に押しつぶされた古い木造古民家の内部をむき出しにする作品を手がけるイギリスの彫刻家アントニー・ゴームリーをはじめ、フランスのコンセプチュアル・アーティストであるアネット・メサジェ、日本の彫刻家である川俣正といった世界的な大物アーティストが参加する予定です。

新潟の長く寒い冬は、日本酒の醸造やその他の発酵文化を育んできました。この地域にはまた、数十種類もの山菜（伝統的に採取されてきた山の新芽や野菜）や、日本でも有数の奥深く美味しい醤油や味噌があります。その伝統が中心となるのが、長岡市に新しくオープンした「発酵の家（Hakko House）」です。シェフの鈴木将氏が手がける11品のコース料理は、季節の食材や山菜を取り入れています。例えば、辛口の発酵ペーストである「なんばんごうじ」でグラッセされたゼンマイや野生のアスパラガス、自家製の麹醤油で味付けされたマグロなどが登場します。それぞれの料理には、シェフが特別に注文した限定の地酒が合わせられています。

鈴木シェフは、新潟の「雪国発酵フード」を扱うショップやレストランのミニ帝国を築いています。その多くは、長岡の1マイル（約1.6キロメートル）に及ぶ「発酵通り（Hakko Trip）」沿いに軒を連ねています。この散策路では、伝統的な味噌蔵、シロップのかかった餅串を提供する歴史ある団子の名店、そして、絶滅しかけた在来米を復活させ、伝統的な「雪室（ゆきむろ）」で仕込み、発酵させ、雪で冷却する酒蔵などに立ち寄ることができます。新潟で長年培われてきたこの技術により、日本酒を摂氏約3度（華氏37度）の低めの温度でじっくりと熟成させることが可能になります。それは、雪国のスローなペースが実に魔法のような結果を生み出すことを思い出させてくれます。――アダム・H・グラハム

今回のデスティネーション・スポットライトでは、新潟の食文化のほか、人気のスキーリゾート、日本トップクラスの海水浴やシュノーケリングなど、その魅力を詳しくご紹介します。

Wednesday Corn & Ethanol Report
Wednesday, October 21, 2026

The agricultural and energy complexes are navigating a fresh wave of seasonal harvest pressure and export demand headwinds this morning, as combines make steady progress across Midwestern fields following last week's USDA WASDE crop revisions. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil continues to trade in a strong elevated corridor near $97.80 to $98.66 per barrel, driven by persistent Middle East transit risks and ongoing logistics friction. Supported by this firm macro energy floor, 44% national harvest completion, and EIA ethanol production rebounding to 1.094 million barrels per day, CBOT corn futures are consolidating in the mid-$4.60 to $4.74 range for December contracts.

Top News Story: Record 16 Billion Bushel Harvest Forecast Weighs on Corn Board

The agricultural trade is continuing to absorb the impact of the USDA's recent WASDE yield update, which raised the estimated national average corn yield to a surprising 181.2 bushels per acre. The 2.7 bushel yield increase driven primarily by unexpected strength across key western Corn Belt states including Nebraska and South Dakota pushed projected U.S. corn production to a massive 16.03 billion bushels and bumped projected ending stocks up to 1.849 billion bushels. While the larger crop estimates sent December futures down from early autumn highs, steady interior processor grinding demand and $98 crude oil are helping establish an active commercial floor as combining reaches its peak seasonal push.

Futures & Market News

CBOT corn futures are trading lower near midday, absorbing heavy harvest hedge pressure and weaker than expected weekly export inspection figures.

December 2026 (Z): $4.66 6/4 (Down 07'4) — testing lower support boundaries as new crop flows accelerate

March 2027 (H): $4.81 2/4 (Down 07'2) — maintaining a modest carry structure

May 2027 (K): $4.89 0/4 (Down 06'6)
Key Driver: Drier field conditions across Iowa, Illinois, and Nebraska have accelerated combine activity, pushing national harvest progress to 44% complete. While recent weak export inspections created near term board drag, $98+ crude oil and firm ethanol plant grinding margins continue to protect interior basis levels.

Commitments of Traders: Funds & Open Interest Deflates

Managed money accounts have moderated their net long positioning in response to seasonal harvest deliveries and softer export inspection totals.

Net Position: Non commercial funds hold a balanced to light net long stance, supported by elevated energy benchmarks and long term commodity index allocation.

Short Covering Surge: Speculative short exposure remains contained, with trading activity largely driven by commercial elevator hedging against physical receipts.

Market Impact: Board liquidity remains solid. Processor bid structures remain protective as refiners work to secure spot bushels against $98+ energy input costs.

USDA Crop Progress: Development Phase
Monday afternoon’s USDA Crop Progress report confirmed that fall harvest activity made solid weekly gains across the Corn Belt.

National Progress: Domestic corn harvest advanced to 44% complete nationwide. Fieldwork continues to lag behind five year averages due to earlier rain delays, but recent clear weather has allowed combines to return at full speed.

Crop Condition: National crop condition ratings for remaining standing fields held steady at 56% good to excellent (with 27% fair and 17% poor/very poor).

State Performance: Combines are advancing quickly across the Central and Western Belt. Early yield and test weight variability remains evident across dryland acres impacted by mid summer heat.

Crop & Weather Update

Domestic Split: Clear, open weather across the Midwest this week is supporting fast harvest progress and field drying. The 6 to 10 day outlook points to near to above normal temperatures, allowing producers to clear fields efficiently before late October rain chances develop.

Nebraska: Harvest is in full swing across Eastern and Central Nebraska. Irrigated fields are delivering solid, resilient yields, while dryland fields continue to reflect test weight drag from summer moisture stress.

International: European corn harvest estimates remain depressed following severe summer heat across Danube basin growing zones. In South America, Brazilian farmers are advancing early first crop corn planting under generally favorable soil moisture conditions.

Ethanol & 45Z Industry News

This morning’s EIA report showed domestic fuel ethanol production rebounding to 1.094 million barrels per day (bpd) for the week ending October 16.

Production Pace: Domestic fuel ethanol output surged to 1.094 million bpd, representing an increase over prior weeks as processing capacity utilization topped 89.8% nationwide.

Inventories & Exports: Overall commercial ethanol inventories rose modestly on the week, though Midwest regional plant inventories dipped as strong domestic blending and steady export demand absorbed plant output.

Cash Impact: Robust refiner processing margins bolstered by WTI crude oil holding near $98.66/barrel are driving ethanol plants to maintain aggressive spot cash bids to secure physical grain.

Natural Gas Trends: The Ethanol "Fuel" Factor

Henry Hub Spot: Trading near $2.88/MMBtu today.

The Trend: Natural gas values remain comfortably anchored below $3.00/MMBtu as steady domestic dry gas production easily matches shoulder season utility demand.

Impact: Low natural gas utility input costs paired with $98+ crude oil are generating strong crush margins for Midwest ethanol processors, allowing plant buyers to aggressively defend local cash basis levels.

The 45Z Regulatory Countdown
The Status: Regulatory teams at the Treasury Department, USDA, and EPA are finalizing administrative protocols for the 45Z clean fuel production credit as harvest deliveries ramp up.

The Focus: Grain trade associations are pushing for immediate operational clarity on software verification tools for sustainable farming practices to prevent terminal delivery friction as farm trucks roll into processors.

Weekly Export Tracker

Weekly Inspections: 672,000 metric tons, reflecting a temporary weekly slowdown compared to trade expectations.

Context: While recent weekly inspection numbers missed analyst targets, cumulative marketing year export commitments maintain a solid pace, anchored by continuous bulk movement to Mexico and Latin American buyers.

Regional Cash Market & Processor Bids

Physical cash corn prices reflect December futures trading at $4.66 6/4. Interior processors and ethanol plants continue to offer protective basis bids to draw spot grain into processing corridors.

National Cash Average: Approximately $4.22 1/2

Central Illinois Average: Basis -0.22 Z | Cash Price $4.44 6/4 (River terminals bidding $4.62 – $4.66 for prompt delivery; Decatur processors holding +0.07 to +0.09 over December futures)
South Central Iowa Average: Basis -0.29 Z | Cash Price $4.37 6/4 (Interior ethanol plant bids remain aggressive to secure spot inventory)

Eastern Nebraska Average: Basis -0.38 Z | Cash Price $4.28 6/4 (Blair and Columbus processing hubs maintaining protective basis postures)

ADM (Decatur, IL): $4.75 Cash | Basis: +0.09 Z
Cargill (Blair, NE): $4.55 Cash | Basis: -0.11 Z

Chief Ethanol (Hastings, NE): $4.40 Cash | Basis: -0.26 Z
Little Sioux (Marcus, IA): $4.35 Cash | Basis: -0.31 Z

Notes: Market Observations & Strategies
Market Observations: WTI crude oil holding near $98.66/barrel, 44% national harvest completion, and EIA weekly ethanol production expanding to 1.094 million bpd have kept December corn supported near $4.66 6/4 despite seasonal hedge pressure and larger USDA crop estimates.

Old Crop Strategy: Ensure any remaining old crop bin inventory is fully delivered to capture current processor crush margins before peak regional harvest receipts hit local elevators.

New Crop Strategy (Z): December corn sitting at $4.66 6/4 provides a solid baseline. Utilize current board levels, market carry, and strong energy tailwinds to execute disciplined target sales during harvest rallies.

text:
🏡 What if the help you need is already living right next door?

Imagine needing a ride to a doctor's appointment, but you don't have transportation.

Imagine needing groceries but having no easy way to get to the store.

Or imagine needing a ladder for just one afternoon, a little help with yard work, or an extra pair of hands to move something heavy.

These might sound like small problems. But for someone facing them, they can turn an ordinary day into a stressful one. ❤️

Now imagine a different situation.

Your neighbor is already driving to Walmart and can give you a ride. Someone nearby has an extra ladder they're happy to lend. Another neighbor has 30 minutes to spare and doesn't mind helping with yard work.

Suddenly, a stressful problem becomes an opportunity for people to connect.

That's the idea behind HelpNearby. 💚

I'm building HelpNearby to make it easier for people to find and offer everyday help within their local communities.

🚗 Need a ride? Connect with neighbors who may be able to help.

🛒 Need help with errands? Someone nearby might be heading in the same direction.

🪜 Need a tool? Maybe someone has one you can borrow instead of buying something you'll rarely use.

🏡 Need a hand around the house? A neighbor might have the time and skills to help.

And if you have time, tools, or skills to share, you can use HelpNearby to offer help to others.

I'm starting this journey in Tooele, Utah, because I believe stronger communities aren't built only through big projects or major investments. They're built through small acts of kindness, trust, and people looking out for one another.

As a software developer and founder, I believe technology should do more than make our lives faster. It should help us solve real problems and bring people closer together.

We have technology connecting us to people thousands of miles away. But sometimes, we still don't know the neighbor living a few houses down.

What if we changed that?

What if asking for help felt a little easier? What if offering help became a natural part of community life? What if we borrowed more, wasted less, and built stronger relationships along the way?

That's the future I'm working toward with HelpNearby.

We're building more than an app. We're working toward a culture where asking for help isn't something to be ashamed of, and offering help is something to be proud of.

💚 Tooele, let's make neighbors helping neighbors a normal part of everyday life.

I'd love to hear your thoughts:

What's one everyday problem you wish it were easier to get help with in your neighborhood? And what skill, tool, or helping hand could you offer someone else?

Let's start the conversation. 👇

#HelpNearby #StartupJourney #CommunityBuilding #TechnologyForGood #TooeleUtah

text:
💔 **She waited for someone who was never coming back.**

At 4:05 on a Sunday afternoon in October, a minivan pulled into a scenic mountain overlook in western Virginia.

A woman stepped out with an elderly beagle, her muzzle gray with age. She walked the dog to a stone railing, tied her leash, and drove away.

By 4:07, the minivan was gone.

**The dog was still waiting.** 💔

For two hours, tourists stopped to admire the beautiful fall colors, completely unaware that an old dog was watching every passing car, waiting for the person she loved to return.

But someone noticed.

His name was Ervin. At 74, he spent his fall weekends selling apples and cider from his pickup truck at that overlook.

When it was time to close, he walked over, untied the trembling old beagle, and offered her water and half his ham sandwich.

She ate every bite, then settled quietly on his tailgate between the baskets of apples.

Stitched into her leash was a single word.

**Maggie.** 🐾

The following weekend, Ervin displayed a picture from the parking lot camera on his apple truck, hoping someone might recognize her.

Hundreds of people saw it.

Nobody came for Maggie.

But here's the beautiful part.

**Maggie doesn't wait by that stone wall anymore.**

These days, she spends her fall weekends riding on Ervin's tailgate, surrounded by apples, cider, and people who stop just to love on her.

Tourists who once came to photograph the changing leaves now take pictures of an old gray-faced beagle.

Someone abandoned Maggie in the mountains because they no longer wanted her.

**But a 74-year-old man selling apples reminded her that she was still worth loving.** ❤️🐾

Sometimes the most beautiful thing you'll find at a scenic overlook isn't the view.

It's the kindness of a stranger who refuses to leave someone behind.

text:
How do you end up looking bigger than your own father in the family portrait? In ancient Egyptian sculpture, you could simply be the person the portrait was made for.

This granodiorite group, carved around 1390 BCE, centers on a priest named Teti. The smaller man beside him is his father, also called Teti; the woman is the elder Teti’s wife, Meket. Their scale expresses the younger Teti’s importance as the statue’s principal owner, while their hands offer supportive gestures. Physical size here communicates a relationship within the monument. An inscription on the central figure’s kilt mentions Ptah, the god of Memphis, suggesting that the group may have been dedicated in a temple there.

Knowing the names completely changes the family photograph: the smaller man is the father. Teti seems to have taken “you’ve grown so much” as a sculptor’s design brief. 😹👪

Photo: Walters Art Museum, Priest Teti with His Family, 22.163. CC0; square crop.

text:
What lesson do we expect the world to draw from Ukraine and North Korea?

Ukraine accepted nuclear disarmament and security assurances. North Korea pursued nuclear weapons as a deterrent. When governments compare those paths, we should worry about the conclusion they might reach. ☢️

📌 1994 — Bill Clinton signed the Budapest Memorandum alongside Russia, the United Kingdom and Ukraine. Ukraine committed to eliminate the nuclear weapons on its territory, accompanied by assurances respecting its sovereignty and existing borders.

These were not NATO-style guarantees requiring America to go to war. Ukraine also did not possess a fully independent, ready-made nuclear deterrent. But the bargain mattered: nuclear disarmament accompanied by international security commitments.

📌 2003 — North Korea announced its withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty during George W. Bush’s presidency.

📌 2006 — North Korea conducted its first nuclear test. Despite sanctions and international opposition, it pursued the ability to threaten catastrophic retaliation.

📌 2008 — Russia invaded Georgia under Bush. In my view, the Western response failed to establish sufficient deterrence against further aggression.

📌 2014 — Russia seized Crimea and intervened in eastern Ukraine under Barack Obama. Joe Biden was vice-president. Both were part of an administration whose response imposed costs but failed to reverse Russia’s territorial gains or prevent subsequent escalation.

📌 2017–2021 — During Donald Trump’s first term, Russia retained Crimea and the war in eastern Ukraine continued. His diplomacy with North Korea did not secure its nuclear disarmament.

📌 2022 — Russia launched its full-scale invasion under President Joe Biden. His administration correctly warned that an invasion was coming, but its warnings and threatened consequences failed to deter Putin.

Biden deserves credit for helping Ukraine resist. He also deserves scrutiny over whether the timing, scale and restrictions on assistance gave Ukraine the strongest possible chance to defend itself. Supporting his decision to provide aid does not require treating every subsequent decision as beyond criticism.

📌 2023–2024 — Trump repeatedly promised to end the war within 24 hours.

📌 2025–2026 — Trump returned to office. His promised rapid resolution remains undelivered.

This is a bipartisan credibility problem. Clinton helped negotiate the security framework. Bush confronted Georgia. Obama and Vice-President Biden confronted Crimea. Trump inherited an ongoing war. President Biden confronted the full-scale invasion. Trump then promised to resolve it.

Different decisions. Different responsibilities. No presidential exemption.

The dangerous inference for other governments is clear: “An agreement leaves us dependent on someone else’s political will. A nuclear arsenal may make attacking us too costly.”

That does not prove nuclear weapons guarantee safety or excuse North Korea’s conduct. It explains why inadequate security assurances can strengthen the case for proliferation.

What could persuade Pyongyang to surrender its deterrent if it believes another administration might reinterpret or abandon the commitments accompanying that decision?

What persuades another country to remain non-nuclear when it watches a nuclear power invade a neighbour whose disarmament it helped negotiate?

Russia bears responsibility for violating its promises and invading Ukraine. America and its allies face a different test: making the commitments underpinning non-proliferation credible enough for others to trust.

How do you persuade countries to honour agreements if your own commitments appear negotiable whenever enforcing them becomes difficult?

Enforcement does not automatically mean American troops. It means sustained consequences for aggression, meaningful support for the injured country and security arrangements that survive elections.

America’s word cannot expire when Clinton leaves, Bush arrives, Obama succeeds him, Trump takes office, Biden replaces him or Trump returns.

If we want fewer countries seeking nuclear weapons, honouring agreements must offer a credible route to security.

Otherwise, we should not be surprised when governments look at Ukraine and North Korea and decide they would rather possess

text:
I am not good with how Democrats conspired to dismantle election integrity in Georgia for the 2020 elections.  By doing this they got Georgia's electoral votes and also snuck in two Senators.   

Mollie Hemingway lays out the scheme here.

‘Sue and Settle’ Smuggles In Major Change to Mail-In

Democrats use various strategies to implement changes to voting laws in order to limit election integrity or make it more difficult for election overseers and observers to detect election fraud. One of the approaches is termed “sue and settle.”

Perkins Coie, the law firm that also ordered what became the Russia collusion hoax against Trump in 2016, runs an extremely well-funded and highly coordinated operation to alter how U.S. elections are run. The firm will sue states and get them to make agreements that alter their voting practices.

Marc Elias, well known for his role in the Russia collusion hoax and other Democrat operations, runs the campaign to change voting laws and practices to favor Democrats. Perkins Coie billed the Democrat Party at least $27 million for its efforts to radically change voting laws ahead of the 2020 election, more than double what they charged Hillary Clinton and the Democratic National Committee for similar work in 2016. Elias was sanctioned in federal court just yesterday for some shenanigans related to a Texas election integrity case.

In March, Raffensperger voluntarily agreed to a settlement in federal court with various Democrat groups, which had sued the state over its rules for absentee voting. The end result was a dramatic alteration in how Georgia conducted the 2020 election.

Republicans were not party to the agreement, despite their huge interest in the case. The agreement explicitly states that neither Raffensperger nor the Democratic groups who sued him take a position on whether the laws and procedures being changed were constitutional or not.

Democrats’ high-powered attorneys introduced several significant changes, such as the opportunity to “cure” ballots. That means that when an absentee ballot comes in with problems that would typically lead it to be trashed, the voter is instead given a chance to “cure” or correct the ballot. It also said Democrats would offer training and guidance on signature verification to county registrars and absentee ballot clerks.

Most importantly, the settlement got rid of any meaningful signature match. The law had previously required signatures to match the signature on file with the Georgia voter registration database. But the settlement allowed the signature to match any signature on file, including the one on the absentee ballot application. That meant a fraudulently obtained ballot would easily have a signature match and no way to detect fraud.

The ballot also could only be rejected if a majority of registrars, deputy registrars, and ballot clerks agreed to it, another burden that made it easier to just let all ballots through without scrutiny. It made a huge difference in how many ballots were rejected.

Raffensperger’s decision to voluntarily agree to such a dramatic change in the rules of the game without input from the Republican Party of Georgia, much less the Republican National Committee, angered many Republicans, including Sens. Kelly Loeffler and David Perdue, as they learned about it following the November 2020 election. Other Republicans felt he harmed election integrity by mailing out millions of absentee ballot applications, ostensibly because of health concerns related to COVID-19.

text:
Young members, students, and emerging professionals gathered at the Fall 2026 ACI Concrete Convention in Atlanta, GA, for a series of events focused on professional development, technical engagement, networking, and opportunities to build lasting connections within the concrete industry.

The weekend began Saturday, October 10, with the ACI Georgia Chapter’s Concrete Kick-Off Event, where approximately 55 young members gathered to watch Atlanta United play. The event provided an informal setting for young professionals to network, strengthen existing relationships, and connect with peers from the local area. The gathering was part of the Student and Young Member Activities Committee’s (SYFAC) continued efforts to support local chapter young member outreach initiatives and encourage greater engagement among emerging professionals.

On Sunday, October 11, SYFAC sponsored the first-ever ACI Technical Committee Fair, featuring representatives from 14 different technical committees. Throughout the day, students, young professionals, and first-time convention attendees had opportunities to speak one-on-one with committee representatives to learn about committee missions, goals, and opportunities to participate and serve. The fair offered attendees a practical introduction to ACI’s technical committee structure and helped connect emerging professionals with opportunities to contribute to the development of industry knowledge, standards, and resources.

On Monday, October 12, the S806 Young Member Activities Committee hosted its annual 'What I Wish I Knew' session, focusing on Emerging Technologies in Concrete. The program featured perspectives from professionals working across construction and concrete technology, highlighting how data science and emerging technologies are influencing the industry.

Nearly 100 attendees participated in the session, including early-career professionals and seasoned industry veterans interested in learning more about the impact of machine learning on concrete construction and related practices. Held each fall, What I Wish I Knew is designed to provide young members with professional development opportunities, practical industry insights, and exposure to emerging topics that can shape their careers.

Also on Monday afternoon, the Young Member Activities Committee presented a mini-session titled A Guide to ACI Documents for Students and Young Professionals. The session offered attendees practical guidance on participating in ACI committee activities and making the most of convention experiences. Together, the presentations encouraged students and young professionals to take advantage of ACI’s technical resources, committee involvement, and professional networking opportunities.

In addition to the educational and networking activities, two young professionals received complimentary convention registration to attend the Atlanta convention through sponsorship from the Women in ACI Committee.

The recipients were:
• Grace Heglas, Structural Engineer at KPFF Consulting Engineers in Nashville, Tennessee.
• Kamilla Wieckowski, Graduate Diagnostics Engineer at Walter P Moore in Chicago, Illinois.

The program helped reduce financial barriers to convention participation and provided both recipients with access to valuable technical programming, professional connections, and career development opportunities.

As the Institute looks ahead to its March 2027 convention in Las Vegas, young professionals have additional opportunities to engage, contribute, and help shape the future of the industry. The S806 Young Member Activities Committee meets twice a year during the ACI Concrete Convention, with its meetings held on Monday afternoons. The committee continues to welcome applications from individuals interested in helping integrate young members into the concrete industry and strengthen engagement across the ACI community.

The committee is also soliciting abstracts for consideration for the Young Member Poster Session at the next ACI Concrete Convention, scheduled for March 21–24, 2027, in Las Vegas, Nevada, USA. ⌛The abstract submission and application for free convention registration are due January 15, 2027.⌛

Young professionals interested in sharing their work, research, or technical insights are encouraged to consider this opportunity to contribute to the convention program and connect with fellow industry professionals. ➡️ Learn more about ACI young member opportunities: https://t.co/5ToG6GFx3T

The Oval Office got crowded on Tuesday. “𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 𝘥𝘢𝘺 𝘰𝘯𝘦 𝘰𝘧 𝘮𝘺 𝘢𝘥𝘮𝘪𝘯𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯, 𝘸𝘦’𝘷𝘦 𝘸𝘢𝘨𝘦𝘥 𝘢𝘯 𝘶𝘯𝘱𝘳𝘦𝘤𝘦𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘸𝘢𝘳 𝘰𝘯 𝘤𝘰𝘳𝘳𝘶𝘱𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘧𝘳𝘢𝘶𝘥, 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘸𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘭𝘦𝘵 𝘰𝘶𝘳 𝘤𝘰𝘶𝘯𝘵𝘳𝘺 𝘣𝘦 𝘭𝘰𝘰𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘱𝘭𝘶𝘯𝘥𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘣𝘺 𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘴, 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘱𝘪𝘳𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘴, 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘧𝘰𝘳𝘦𝘪𝘨𝘯 𝘧𝘳𝘢𝘶𝘥𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘴—𝘢𝘯𝘥, 𝘣𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘭𝘭𝘺, 𝘴𝘤𝘶𝘮,” President Trump said, flanked by JD Vance, FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Dr. Mehmet Oz and Stephen Miller.

Then he unveiled the mechanism: the new Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program (WHIP) pays ordinary citizens $𝟏𝟎,𝟎𝟎𝟎 𝐭𝐨 $𝟑𝟎,𝟎𝟎𝟎 for tips that lead to criminal fraud charges, plus a potential 𝟏% 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 on whatever money the government actually recovers.

“𝘐𝘧 𝘪𝘵’𝘴 $10 𝘮𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯, $200 𝘮𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯, $400 𝘮𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯—𝘸𝘦’𝘳𝘦 𝘨𝘪𝘷𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢 1% 𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘴𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘵𝘰 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘴𝘰𝘯,” Trump said. Most existing federal whistleblower programs don’t pay out until a case is fully resolved, sometimes years later. @authorlilyriley
