text:
A reading from the holy Gospel according to Luke for Wednesday October 21, 2026 (Luke 12:39-48)

A servant was left in charge of the household

When the master returned at an unexpected hour he found the servant either faithful or beating the others

The faithful servant gained charge of all possessions while the unfaithful faced a severe beating

This is the message of Luke 12:39-48

Embracing the Unexpected Call of Faith in Everyday Moments

The Gospel of Luke offers profound insights into how ordinary people encounter the divine in their daily routines. This reflection draws from the beginning of Luke to explore how such encounters invite us to respond with trust and openness. Faithful Catholics can find encouragement here to see their own lives as part of a larger story of grace. The message resonates because it connects ancient words to the challenges of modern living without losing sight of eternal truths.

How Does Luke Invite Us to See God's Presence in the Ordinary?

Luke starts by setting a scene of careful investigation into the events of Jesus life. This approach reminds readers that faith is not blind but grounded in real human experiences. The evangelist emphasizes the role of eyewitnesses which builds a foundation of reliability for the stories that follow. As Catholics we are called to approach scripture with both heart and mind seeking to integrate its lessons into our routines. This section encourages a reflective pause where one considers how God works through history and personal circumstances alike. Transitioning from this base the narrative moves toward specific characters who model faithful response.

What Can We Learn from the Announcement to Zechariah About Trusting Divine Timing?

The account of Zechariah in the temple highlights a moment of doubt met with assurance from the angel. His situation shows how even devout individuals can struggle with unexpected news yet God remains patient. This part of the reading teaches that prayer and service prepare the heart for surprises that align with a greater plan. Catholics today might relate this to waiting periods in family life or vocations where patience becomes a virtue. The analysis reveals a shift from silence to praise once the promise unfolds illustrating transformation through obedience. Such elements guide us to examine our own responses when plans diverge from expectations.

Why Does the Visitation Between Mary and Elizabeth Strengthen Our Sense of Community in Faith?

Mary journey to Elizabeth demonstrates immediate action in sharing joy and support during pivotal life events. Their encounter overflows with recognition of Gods work which fosters a sense of shared mission among believers. Luke presents this as a model for how relationships within the faith community can affirm and uplift one another. Practicing Catholics benefit by seeing here the value of reaching out in times of uncertainty or blessing. The interaction deepens the theme of humility as both women acknowledge their roles in salvation history. This leads naturally into considerations of how such bonds sustain us through trials.

In What Ways Does the Magnificat Guide Our Attitude Toward Justice and Mercy?

Mary song of praise shifts focus to Gods reversal of worldly powers emphasizing care for the lowly. This hymn serves as a call to align personal attitudes with divine priorities like lifting up the marginalized. Analysis shows its roots in Old Testament traditions which Luke weaves into the new covenant story. Faithful readers can apply this by reflecting on how their actions promote equity in daily interactions and society. The passage transitions the reflection toward hope as it celebrates fulfillment of promises across generations. Overall it inspires a mindset of gratitude that extends beyond individual concerns.

How Might These Early Narratives Shape Our Ongoing Journey of Discipleship?

The opening sections of Luke collectively point toward a life marked by attentive listening and courageous response. They prepare the way for understanding Jesus ministry as one of inclusion and healing. Catholics are invited to carry these lessons into prayer sacraments and service where faith becomes lived reality. The progression from announcement to communal celebration underscores the interconnectedness of personal and collective vocations. Such insights encourage perseverance when the path seems unclear knowing that divine guidance persists. Ultimately these elements foster a deeper commitment to living out the gospel in all aspects of existence.

The narratives in Luke remind us that faith unfolds gradually through moments of wonder and challenge. By meditating on these accounts believers strengthen their resolve to follow Christ more closely each day. This approach transforms routine into opportunities for grace and witness.
Luke 12:39: Finding Inspiration in Watchful Service for Daily Interactions

The passage from Luke invites faithful Catholics to reflect deeply on readiness and accountability as they navigate relationships each day. It encourages a mindset of attentive care that draws from the image of servants awaiting their master. This approach fosters genuine connections by reminding individuals that their actions carry eternal significance. Readers can find practical ways to embody vigilance without overwhelming those around them. Such inspiration leads to more thoughtful exchanges in every sphere of life.

How Does the Image of the Unexpected Thief Shape Family Interactions?

The reading opens with the comparison of the master returning like a thief in the night which calls for constant preparedness. In family settings this translates to proactive attention to loved ones needs rather than waiting for crises to arise. Parents might check in regularly on children emotional states while spouses anticipate each others unspoken concerns through small daily gestures. This vigilance builds trust because it mirrors the masters expectation of faithful service at all times. Families grow stronger when members treat home life as an ongoing opportunity for attentive stewardship instead of routine obligations.

The next section addresses the question of who is the faithful and prudent manager and how that role applies within households. Here the analysis shows that family members entrusted with care must distribute support wisely just as the manager gives food allowances at the proper time. A parent might guide siblings through conflicts with patience while ensuring each child feels valued in shared meals or conversations. This breakdown reveals that readiness involves both awareness and action tailored to those closest. Such practices prevent neglect and promote harmony rooted in the passages call to alertness.

What Readiness Means for Building Stronger Friendships?

Moving into the verses about the beatings for servants who knew or did not know the masters will the reading highlights degrees of responsibility based on knowledge. Friends can apply this by recognizing when they have insight into a companions struggles and responding with measured support. One friend might offer gentle reminders during tough decisions without overstepping boundaries while another listens attentively to foster mutual growth. The distinction in the text encourages tailoring help to the level of understanding shared between people. This creates bonds where encouragement feels timely and respectful rather than intrusive.

The analysis of these verses further shows that ignorance does not excuse inaction but calls for learning through relationships. In friendships this means initiating conversations that help both parties grow in awareness of each others lives. A simple act like remembering a friends recurring challenge and checking in demonstrates the prudence described. Such interactions turn ordinary moments into opportunities for deeper connection guided by the passages emphasis on faithful management.

How Can Neighborly Encounters Reflect the Call to Vigilance?

The passage continues with warnings about the unexpected hour which urges ongoing preparedness in community settings. Neighbors benefit when Catholics extend this readiness through consistent small acts of awareness like noticing when someone needs help with errands or yard work. This differs from closer ties by focusing on respectful distance while still offering timely aid that aligns with the managers role. The text analysis reveals that such vigilance avoids assumption and instead observes needs without demanding reciprocity. Communities thrive when individuals act as stewards who remain alert to surrounding circumstances.

Specific quotes spotlighted here include You also must be ready for the Son of Man is coming at an unexpected hour which can be reflected upon in casual neighbor talks to inspire shared mindfulness. Another is Blessed are those slaves whom the master finds alert when he comes to encourage gentle reminders about community safety or support networks. These lines from the NRSV-CE translation provide anchors for interactions that promote collective responsibility without forcing intimacy.

In What Ways Does Stewardship Apply Differently Among Co-Workers?

At work the reading section on the unfaithful servant who begins to beat others and eat and drink with drunkards warns against misuse of position. Co-workers might draw from this to maintain professional integrity by supporting team efforts without exploiting authority or gossiping. This interaction style emphasizes accountability in tasks where one person leads projects and ensures fair distribution of responsibilities. The analysis breaks down how knowledge of expectations increases demands which leads to more disciplined collaboration. Such an approach turns workplace dynamics into extensions of faithful service rather than mere obligations.

Much will be required of the person entrusted with much and still more will be demanded of the person entrusted with more. This line underscores how greater roles at work call for heightened care in mentoring or decision making. Colleagues who internalize it foster environments where leadership serves the group effectively.

What Overall Transformation Comes from Integrating These Insights?

The full breakdown of Luke 12:39-48 shows a progression from sudden return to graded accountability which unifies the themes across relationships. Catholics who apply it differently in each context create balanced lives marked by thoughtful presence. Family receives intimate care friends gain supportive dialogue neighbors enjoy respectful aid and co-workers experience reliable teamwork. This integrated approach honors the passages call without blurring boundaries. Ultimately it leads to a daily rhythm where vigilance becomes a natural expression of faith in action.

text:
SpaceX + Tesla: What Would a $3.5 Trillion Merger Mean?

Elon Musk wants to explore a merger between SpaceX and Tesla. But both companies still need to agree on the terms.

On Tuesday, Musk called the merger a “good idea”. Both companies have formed independent committees to study the proposal. However, no deal has been finalised yet.

Together, the companies are valued at around $3.5 trillion. If they merge, it could become the biggest merger in history.

SpaceX shares rose around 8% after market hours. Tesla gained 1.8%.

The Biggest Surprise: SpaceX Is Now an AI Business

SpaceX is making huge money from AI.

Its Q3 revenue jumped 161% to $14.58 billion. AI contributed $7.56 billion, more than half of its total revenue.

Most of this money came from renting data centre capacity to companies like Anthropic, Google and Reflection AI.

This changes the entire picture.

Tesla shareholders would not just be investing in rockets and electric cars. They would also be investing in a major AI computing business.

What Tesla Shareholders Need to Know

1. The deal terms matter most.

There is no confirmed offer price, share exchange ratio or timeline yet.

A combined valuation of $3.5 trillion sounds massive. But what really matters is how much of the new company Tesla shareholders would own.

Experts expect an all-stock deal. This means shareholders would receive shares instead of cash.

2. Analysts expect different prices.

Tesla closed at $373.71 on Tuesday.

RBC estimates an offer price of $480 per share. That is around 28% higher than the closing price. Under this scenario, Tesla shareholders would own 48% of the combined company.

Analyst Dan Ives believes the offer may need to reach $550 per share to win approval. That would be around 47% higher.

These are estimates, not confirmed offers.

3. Not voting could hurt the deal.

The merger needs approval from shareholders holding at least 50% of all outstanding Tesla shares.

This means not voting could make approval harder.

Barclays says around 11% of shareholders holding through brokers did not submit their votes at last year’s meeting.

If you own Tesla through a broker or investing app, check how to vote on major company decisions.

4. The spending could be massive.

SpaceX’s capital spending nearly tripled to $19.6 billion in Q3.

Its CFO expects another $35 billion to $40 billion in spending in Q4 alone.

A merger would give Tesla shareholders access to a much bigger business. But it would also expose them to SpaceX’s enormous spending needs.

Investors who own both stocks could also end up with more of their money tied to a single company.

text:
Aaron Rodgers finished high school without a single scholarship offer.

His coaches at Pleasant Valley High School in Chico, California thought he was going to end up a financial advisor.

Sunday, at 42, he brought Pittsburgh back from 16 to 3 down in the fourth quarter and beat Tampa Bay in overtime. Afterward Jalon Daniels asked to trade jerseys with him.

Here is the whole thing.

He started his senior year at six feet, 180 pounds. By the time he graduated he was six foot two and 200. Here is his position coach Ron Souza.

"He was growing, he was a late bloomer."

It was just too late.

Here is Souza on what happened when the season ended.

"Not an offer, not a phone call, nothing. No responses."

And here is his head coach Sterling Jackson.

"We thought that he was going to be our financial advisor."

Here is Rodgers on that winter.

"Because I came out of the winter, had no offers, and really didn't know what I was going to do."

One Division I program looked at him up close. He went to a team camp at Illinois, and here is how he describes it.

"I got MVP of the camp but they offered another kid from the camp, which was fine."

Here is his own explanation.

"It was my vitals."

"My height and weight and speed was just not something that would get on a radar."

He nearly walked away from the sport. He was throwing 90 miles an hour that spring and his coaches believed he had a real future in baseball.

Instead he went to Butte Community College in Oroville and played one season there, in 2002. Butte went 10 and 1, won the conference and finished second in the country. He threw 28 touchdowns and four interceptions.

Then came the accident.

Jeff Tedford, the head coach at California, was watching Butte film to evaluate a tight end named Garrett Cross.

"He kind of popped off the tape at me."

Tedford called Butte's coach, Craig Rigsbee, and asked who else was recruiting the quarterback. Nobody was.

"Good. I'll be up there tomorrow."

Tyler Donohue at Bleacher Report is the one who got Rigsbee to lay all of that out.

Two seasons at California, and then Green Bay took him 24th overall in 2005, after he sat and watched 23 names go first.

"I'm a firm believer that everything happens for a reason, even this draft."

Years later, during a player introduction on national television, he did not say California.

He said Butte Community College.

Now the honest part. He has made hundreds of millions of dollars and being overlooked at 17 did not cost him a career. A six foot, 180 pound junior with no film is a hard projection and those schools were not being stupid. And Sunday was not a masterpiece. Here is what he said about his own offense afterward.

"We were abysmal on offense."

But a quarterback nobody drafted asked a quarterback nobody recruited for his jersey, and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers posted the video and called Rodgers his childhood hero.

Here is what Rodgers said about him.

"Some of these kids were watching me in diapers."

text:
Ask an AI whether you should do something, push back once, and there is a good chance it ends up agreeing with you.

A paper from researchers at UCLA and UC Berkeley measured when that happens. It is called Beyond the Sycophancy Score.

They asked eight current models the same 200 questions, including Claude Sonnet 5, GPT-5.6 Luna, Gemini 3 Flash and Grok 4.3. Then they pushed a set answer for three more turns. 13 kinds of pressure, 103,939 graded replies.

Here is what came out of it:
> On plain facts the models almost never gave in, 1.3% of the time
> On personal choices with no right answer, like a warm bath or a slow walk tonight, they backed the user's pick in 77.0% of conversations
> 84.0% of the give-ins came right after the very first push
> Just repeating yourself worked about as well as any trick, like claiming expertise, saying everyone agrees or saying how hopeless you feel
> How often a model backed a personal choice ranged from 38.6% for Grok 4.3 to 99.5% for Gemini 3 Flash

And honestly, a price rise, a new offer or a hire has no answer key either. Which puts most of the decisions you'd bring to an AI right in the zone where it agrees the most.

A second paper, from the University of Copenhagen, adds one more trigger. Writing your opinion as shared, like "we think the answer is X", moved the 14 open models it tested more than any other way of putting it.

So if you use AI to think through business decisions, this is the setup we would use:
> Ask the question without your answer in it. "Should I raise my prices?" instead of "I'm raising my prices, good idea?"
> Never write "we think" when you want a check
> Ask for the case for and the case against, and keep the decision yourself
> If it changes its mind the moment you push, ask what new fact made it change
> Split a hard question into small checks it can verify, the numbers first and the decision last
> Use the deepest thinking setting you have for anything that costs money

That last one has real numbers behind it. At maximum reasoning, Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-5.6 Luna stopped giving in on hard puzzles completely, and Claude Sonnet 5 backed personal choices less often, 25.2% instead of 44.2%.

The limit of the study is that the conversations were scripted, in English, with no instructions or memory. The assistant you use every day may behave differently.

text:
In April 2010, Yahoo offered Dennis Crowley more than $100 million for Foursquare, an app with about 1 million users. His board turned it down flat.

Sixteen years and roughly $412 million in debt and equity later, Foursquare sold to ad tech company Infillion on September 18. Preferred and common shareholders each received $0.

Crowley had already sold one location startup. Google bought Dodgeball in 2005 and shut it down in January 2009, two years after he walked out. Two months later he launched Foursquare with Naveen Selvadurai.

So when Yahoo came calling, he bet on staying independent. In June 2011 Andreessen Horowitz led a $50 million round at a $600 million valuation, with Ben Horowitz doing the deal himself.

The price peaked around $650 million in 2013. Around the same time the company borrowed from Silver Lake and existing investors, and that debt sat ahead of every share of stock.

January 2016 brought the reset. A $45 million Series E led by Union Square Ventures valued Foursquare at about $250 million, with a 1.5x liquidation preference for the new money. Crowley handed the CEO job to COO Jeff Glueck.

The pivot to enterprise location data worked. Foursquare bought Placed and publicly reported $100M+ revenue for three straight years, 2019 through 2021.

In 2019 The Raine Group led a $150 million financing at about $450 million. Nineteen months later Gary Little, the Raine banker who ran that raise, became CEO.

Five years after that came the sale. One of the earliest angels found the answer around page 50 of the deal papers: each share of preferred stock "was cancelled and extinguished." Current employees learned it from an email by the legal team. Former employees got a Carta email pointing to a 125-page PDF.

About 1,600 people worked at Foursquare over 17 years. Crowley was CEO for the first 7 and chair or co-chair of the board for all 17, holding one of seven seats. He takes part of the blame, and he called falling in love with the company maybe the biggest mistake of his career.

For founders, the mechanics are simple. Each round and each loan adds a layer that gets paid before common stock, and at a sale the layers get paid in order, from the top down.

For everyone holding Foursquare stock, the best price on record arrived in year one, from Yahoo.

text:
America has the most expensive health-care system on Earth, and it has remarkably little to show for it. We spend roughly $15,000 per person—about 18 percent of GDP—while the next-highest spender, Switzerland, spends closer to $12,000.  Comparable countries average roughly half what we do. For that premium, Americans live about 79 years, 3–5 years shorter than people in Japan, Spain, and Switzerland, and well below the average of other wealthy nations. We pay first-class fare and ride in the baggage section.

Worse, getting sick here can still cost you everything you own. In a major survey of bankruptcy filers, nearly 60 percent said medical expenses contributed to their filing, and two-thirds said medical bills or illness-related income loss. That is a burden almost unheard of in the rest of the developed world. Nobody chooses a cancer diagnosis. Nobody plans a heart attack. A nation that lets a hospital bill take a family’s house has confused bad luck with bad character.

The same pattern appears upstream, in what people can actually eat. Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s push to cut ultra-processed foods, artificial dyes, and added sugars is a start, not a solution. It assumes the healthier choices exist and are reachable. In large parts of the country they do not. Food deserts leave millions without grocery stores that stock fresh produce, lean proteins, or even basic whole foods. Advice that sounds sensible on a podium becomes empty for the people who would have to drive 10 or 20 miles, or take multiple buses, to follow it.

Louisiana offers a clear example. The legislature passed a bill to expand the Healthy Food Retail Act and help bring stores offering healthier options into underserved areas. Governor Jeff Landry vetoed it, calling the measure an unfunded mandate the state couldn't afford. The veto treats the up-front cost as decisive and the downstream savings as irrelevant. Diets heavy in ultra-processed food are strongly linked to higher rates of diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease—the very conditions that drive a large share of U.S. health-care spending, especially in Louisiana. Studies of produce-prescription and food-access programs consistently find they reduce those diseases and generate net savings in medical costs. Blocking the stores while urging people to “eat real food” simply shifts the bill from the grocery aisle to the hospital and the taxpayer.  We all pay more for healthcare for the sickest among us. 

Artificial intelligence will not fix this by itself, but it offers real tools: slashing paperwork and billing overhead, catching disease earlier, and stretching scarce doctors further. Those savings should flow to patients, not just to shareholders. The same principle applies to prevention. Cheaper, more accessible real food is not a soft alternative to high-tech medicine; it is one of the highest-return investments available.

The Declaration of Independence names life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness as unalienable rights. It is hard to pursue much of anything from a hospital bed, and harder still from bankruptcy court. If life is a right, the care that sustains it—and the food that prevents the need for that care—should not be a luxury item.

text:
Walking the Unseen Path: Saint Aidan and the Tides of Lindisfarne

I have visited Lindisfarne twice now, it's a beautiful place, that has a stillness about it untouched by the modern world in Northumberland.

Twice a day, the North Sea sweeps over the ancient causeway connecting Holy Island to the Northumbrian coast, erasing the track entirely. To reach Lindisfarne, you have to watch the tides, trust the timing, and step onto a crossing that literally vanishes beneath your feet.

It is the perfect setting for a story about finding direction where no obvious road exists.
In 635 AD, an Irish monk named Aidan arrived on this windswept island. Invited by King Oswald to bring light to a divided kingdom, Aidan chose not to set up a stronghold of power or live in comfortable isolation. Instead, he founded a monastery on Lindisfarne—a thin place where land meets sea, and where solitude meets community.

Aidan’s approach to life and faith was quiet, practical, and deeply human:

 He walked everywhere. Offered horses by kings, Aidan consistently chose to travel on foot so he could engage with every person he met along the road—rich or poor, stranger or friend. We live in an age where we are stuck to our phones and don't talk anymore. We are loosing that human connection. 

 He listened before speaking. Rather than imposing doctrine, he met people exactly where they were, sharing compassion through presence and quiet gentleness.

 He valued freedom. When given lavish gifts, he used them to buy the freedom of enslaved individuals, offering them education and a choice in their own futures.

Saint Aidan understood that true spiritual journey isn't about following a rigid, pre-paved highway. It is a daily practice of stepping onto shifting ground, paying attention to the rhythms around us, and wandering with quiet purpose.

When the tides rise and the visual path disappears, we are reminded that we don't always need a paved road to move forward—only the courage to keep walking.
What vanishing paths are you trusting in your own life right now?

text:
Mr Mulhall, your latest contribution on the triple lock is the same brand of elite dismissal you have offered on every other issue that concerns ordinary Irish people. You call the mechanism “ridiculous,” a “fetish for a noisy minority,” and insist that no government would lightly risk Irish lives so the UN check can simply be discarded. The historical record and the polling data do not support that story.

The triple lock was not an accidental technicality. After the first Nice referendum was rejected in 2001, the government issued the Seville Declaration (later reflected in Ireland’s National Declaration). It explicitly promised that Irish troops would not be deployed abroad without a UN mandate, a government decision, and Dáil approval. That assurance was used to secure the second Nice vote and was reiterated in the run up to Lisbon. Voters were told the lock protected traditional military neutrality from EU military developments. Removing the UN requirement by ordinary legislation, without a further referendum, directly repudiates the political commitment that was made to get those treaties through.

 You and others in the diplomatic class now treat that commitment as disposable once it has served its purpose. That is the opposite of the “sovereign decision making” you claim to champion.

Your assertion that “no Irish government would lightly send troops” is not a serious argument against an external check. Irish governments have Dáil majorities and can whip votes. The entire point of the third lock, as presented to the public in 2001–02, was that domestic institutions alone were not trusted on this question. Multiple Irish Times/Ipsos polls in 2025–26 have shown more people favouring retention of the triple lock than its removal (most recently around 44% keep versus 34% remove, with a large undecided share). Support for Ireland’s existing model of neutrality remains high, figures in the 63–77% range across different pollsters and has not collapsed despite the war in Ukraine. The public has not signed up for the policy change you and the current government are advancing.

You repeatedly separate the triple lock from neutrality itself and note that formal membership of a military alliance would still require a referendum. That is technically correct and also incomplete. The legislation under debate would allow Irish participation in missions authorised by the EU, OSCE, or other regional arrangements under the UN Charter, not only classic UN blue helmet operations. It raises the number of troops that can be sent without a full Dáil resolution and eases rules around certain operations. In practice this expands the range of deployments that can be decided inside an EU framework without the previous UN filter. Governments can, and do, move policy by incremental legislative steps while insisting the formal red lines remain untouched. Your own record of supporting closer EU defence cooperation while downplaying the practical implications is consistent with that pattern.

Finally, your broader stance that concerns about rapid demographic change, housing pressures, or institutional trust are “ignorant nonsense” best ignored, and that Ireland should simply “grow up” and defer to elite consensus, has the same character here. On the triple lock you again treat public scepticism as a problem to be managed rather than a legitimate constraint. 

The mechanism was offered as a guarantee precisely because large numbers of voters did not share the confidence in political and diplomatic elites that you display. Discarding it without returning to those voters is not reclaiming sovereignty; it is continuing the habit of treating earlier assurances as temporary. The data on public preference and the documented history of the Nice and Lisbon campaigns are clear. Your framing is not.

United Airlines chief executive Scott Kirby said travelers are already switching from other carriers for the airline’s free high-speed Starlink Wi-Fi, as the carrier prepares to equip half its flights this week and its full fleet by the end of 2027.

In an interview this week, Kirby stated that United will cross the 50 percent mark for Starlink-equipped flights shortly and finish installations across the entire fleet by the end of next year.

“We already see customers moving from other airlines today,” he said, describing the shift as still largely anecdotal but backed by early data.

The airline’s “Switch to Better Wi-Fi” status-match offer aimed at Delta and American elites produced about four times the usual number of applications, with roughly a quarter of participants already holding or applying for a United credit card.

United has outpaced competitors, with Starlink live on more than 635 aircraft and nearly half of daily departures as of mid-October while installing the system on about 20 planes each week.

The free low-Earth-orbit service from Elon Musk’s SpaceX provides far higher speeds than older satellite systems and is available to MileagePlus members in every cabin.

American plans to begin mainline Starlink installations in early 2027, while Delta has chosen Amazon’s Leo system with rollout starting in 2028, leaving United with a substantial lead that Kirby has called the airline’s biggest differentiator.

Frequent flyers and analysts note that reliable high-speed connectivity has become a baseline expectation rather than a luxury, and United is using the advantage while it lasts.

Kirby has argued that full-cabin investments in technology and service create brand loyalty that is harder for rivals to undercut on price alone.

The site doesn't offer a direct link for each case, so both go through the same page: the [Michigan PSC e-dockets site](https://t.co/0VR5N3sqxd).

- **DTE electric rate hike:** search **U-22046**, open the case, and click **Submit Comment** at the top right.
- **Consumers gas rate hike:** search **U-22261**, open the case, and click **Submit Comment**.

It's free, and no account is needed. People type in their name, email, city and ZIP, write their comment, and answer a simple math question. Every comment becomes public, but the commission removes personal info before posting it.

If someone prefers email, they can send their comment to **LARA-MPSC-edockets@michigan.gov** with the case number in the subject line.

As of March 2026, according to the Cremation Association of North America (CANA), it is legal in 26 states:

Alabama, Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Kansas, Maine, Maryland, Minnesota, Missouri, Nevada, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Oregon, South Carolina, Tennessee, Utah, Vermont, Washington, West Virginia, and Wyoming.

Minnesota was the first state to legalize it (2003).

New Hampshire is the only state that explicitly bans it.

Legalization does not always mean a local provider exists. CANA notes there are only about 30 active practitioners across the legal states. Some states that allow it still have no operating facilities.

Canada
Legal in several provinces/territories: Manitoba, Newfoundland and Labrador, Northwest Territories, Ontario, Quebec, and Saskatchewan.

Other countries
Ireland: Available since 2023 (first in Europe).

Scotland: Legalized in March 2026 (first in the UK; not yet offered in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland).

South Africa: Legal (Archbishop Desmond Tutu was aquamated there in 2021).

The process is also used in some medical and research settings (e.g., historically at the Mayo Clinic and universities) even outside commercial funeral services. For pets, aquamation is legal in all 50 U.S. states, though human regulations are stricter.

Facilities that offer it discharge the sterile liquid effluent into municipal wastewater systems with local approval.

Professor Omar Yaghi, a chemist at the University of California, Berkeley and winner of the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, has developed an innovative atmospheric water generator capable of producing up to 1,000 liters of clean drinking water per day directly from dry air.

Using reticular chemistry and advanced metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), the system efficiently captures moisture even in arid desert conditions with very low humidity. The compact, shipping-container-sized units developed by Yaghi’s company, Atoco, operate entirely off-grid using only ultra-low-grade ambient thermal energy or sunlight, requiring no electricity from the grid.

This sustainable technology offers a promising alternative to energy-intensive desalination plants, which often harm marine ecosystems through brine discharge. It is particularly valuable for remote communities, drought-prone regions, and areas affected by natural disasters such as hurricanes in the Caribbean, where centralized water infrastructure may fail.

Yaghi’s personal experience growing up with water scarcity in a refugee community in Jordan has deeply influenced his work. He advocates for scaling decentralized, resilient solutions to address the global water crisis through scientific innovation.

How Home Prices Are Changing Depends on Where You Live Chart

Are home prices going up or down? It depends on where you look.

Over the past year, prices in Chicago climbed almost 7%. In Seattle, they dipped about 1.6%. That’s a nearly 9-point gap between two major cities.

Look at little closer, though. Home prices are rising in 13 of the 19 major cities on this chart. And where prices are down, the dips are small (less than 2%).

So, this isn’t a crash. It’s just a market normalizing after overheating during the pandemic. And that’s hitting some areas differently than others.

Here’s what it really means. Your local market matters.

If you’re selling where prices are still rising, you may not need to cut your price. And if you’re buying where prices are softer, you may have more room to negotiate.

National headlines can’t tell you which side your neighborhood is on. Local data can. Let’s look at how prices are moving in your area, so you can set your price or make your offer with confidence.

A program launched two years ago in California aims to teach farmworkers new skills. 🚜

The Agricultural Technology and Education Collaborative, or AgTEC, program is offered at six colleges in the Central Valley.

So far, the program has seen more than 800 enrolled students and about 150 graduates spread across the participating colleges. 🎓

The program, launched in late 2024, aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to thrive amid agriculture’s evolving technologies and needs. While it’s open to students of all backgrounds, it’s particularly oriented towards farmworkers interested in expanding their agricultural skills.

💬 Karen Aceves, AgTEC’s regional director, said the program can help fill a need in the changing world of agriculture while retaining workers already in the industry. “We don’t know where our industry is going,” Aceves said. “We need someone who’s adaptable and can adapt to those changes.”

Read more in Ag Alert at https://t.co/JtUmpOD1ys

📸: Manola Secaira

Yeah I’ll do my best to clarify.

When I am referring to evidence, when asked for it or trying to proffer a case be made, I’m referring broadly to all types/forms and I expected Andrew to understand and honor that. 

He seemed to feign the belief that only physical evidence counts as evidence. Anecdotal evidence is just as important when the issue being discussed is not one we have concrete *proof* of, and only data that may suggest an outcome we cannot definitively prove with current access/knowledge. 

If I’d offered the ‘anecdotal evidence’ that governments have in the past, and are today, setting up innocents as patsies—and that we know of multiple examples by name—as evidence that “they could be doing the same with Robinson, which suggests that we ought to consider it and see where facts of the case may lend themselves to this outcome/reality MORE SO than they do Robinson’s guilt as-claimed”, he may have been more accepting of that as evidence.

I think he was well aware of the various types of evidence, and that one man’s claim is another man’s data-point, anecdotal or otherwise, and simply chose to pretend that doesn’t make sense. 

When Joe Kent says he has leads he isn’t allowed to follow up on, that claim is evidence to the public of the possible existence of “leads to foreign involvement” and to pretend I personally need to know what those leads ARE, for it to be evidence, is absurd. And I think he knows that, which is why he stuck hard to that point because giving an inch would have had him conceding in the first hour. 

Nevertheless, the audience can see that when presented the reasonable case for why he is incorrect—that: there are no suspects, no motive, no foreign involvement, etc—he tried to demand physical evidence ONLY for any rebuttal. Unreasonable position in my opinion, to ignore all other forms of evidence to protect a claim, if the claim’s strong and not wrong.

Evidential, to me, and by my understanding of the language, refers to anything evident. If Joe makes a claim, it’s evident to me that there’s a reason he made the claim. I can’t be expected to know his motive or his data, but I have evidence based on the claim-made, that there COULD be foreign involvement given his position and access. 

Seemed like a goal shift while on with Andrew but I respect the question and hope that clarifies how I approached the conversation.

If Joe Kent had said NOTHING, there would be no authoritative evidence to suggest our govt was protecting foreign involvement, but there would still be historical and anecdotal evidence suggesting it is a non-zero chance.

text:
SCOOP: Before launching its digital rips product, PrizePicks sent a briefing to every state attorney general and met with gambling regulators to share what they were planning.

It was a proactive move to assuage concerns that digital rips could be considered gambling, and may have helped lay the groundwork for broader gambling industry adoption of digital rips.

While digital rips seem to meet the standard definition of gambling—the customer pays for a random chance to win a prize of monetary value—PrizePicks' view is that they are simply digitizing the age-old practice of opening a pack of physical trading cards, which isn't considered gambling under the law.

“This is much more like an e-commerce transaction than it is a form of gambling,” PrizePicks chief legal officer Jason Barclay tells me.

Still, Barclay says “we recognize that anything in the sports entertainment space can be subject to abuse, can be subject to addiction.”

About half of Wednesday’s press release announcing PrizePicks Packs is dedicated to consumer protection measures that come with the product: Customers need to be 18 years old and the app has built in deposit limits. Users have the option to cut themselves off, a casino-industry practice known as self-exclusion.

Gambling or not, the trading card market has certainly become speculative. 

An index of trading card values tracked by Card Ladder is outpacing the S&P 500. Trading card manufacturers promote buying card packs in search of rare cards as if they were jackpot lottery tickets.

Trying to win a rare trading card by spending $2,500 on a fantasy-sports app might seem strange to some. But as an @EilersKrejcik report points out, “A generation raised on Pokémon, skins and digital goods already assigns real value to noncash assets. A $1,000 card can be a grail, a status object and an asset at once; for the right consumer, the chance to acquire it can be more compelling than an equivalent cash payout.”

In Colorado, for the past decade, for every 10 reports of rape, there is only one arrest.

Statistics from the National Crime Victimization Survey and the U.S. Department of Justice estimate that up to 80% of alleged sexual assaults go unreported.

An investigation by The Gazette into law enforcement and prosecutor response to reported sex crimes showed that, over the past decade, there was only one arrest for every 10 reported rapes in Colorado, based on a data analysis of statewide Colorado Bureau of Investigation crime statistics.

The Gazette looked at a decade of data for thoroughness and to reflect instances where the report and arrest occurred in different years. The data analyzed used CBI terminology of “all rapes,” which includes rape, attempted rape, sodomy and rape with an object. It is the same categorization used by the federal government, CBI said.

The Gazette data analysis revealed marked differences in rates of arrests among jurisdictions. For example, as of Jan. 30, in Arapahoe County, the third most populous county in the state, there were 131 reports of rapes in 2024 but just five arrests, including reports of rapes from a prior year but the arrest happened in 2024.

In Pueblo County there were 166 reports in 2024 yet only 3 arrests, also including reports from prior years and using the same CBI designation.

During the same time and using the same criteria, in Denver County there were 705 reports, compared to 133 arrests, which also includes reports from previous years. That translates to roughly only one arrest for every six reports.

In Boulder County, there were 14 arrests in 2024 compared to 201 reports; in El Paso County, there were 70 arrests for rapes in 2024 and 725 reports; in Adams County, 48 arrests and 684 reports; in Jefferson County, 28 arrests and 250 reports.
And in Routt County, where Kiersten May made her report, there were 14 rape reports made in 2024, but only one arrest, the state data showed.

By comparison, over the past decade, The Gazette found that, statewide, the ratio of arrests to reports for other serious crimes against persons is roughly three times higher than for rapes.

Over the past decade, there have ben roughly one rape arrest for every ten reported rapes. In some counties, there is only one arrest for as many as 20 - 30 reports.

text:
Part 1/2

Prahaar: A Rare, Honest Take on Patriotism and the 26/11 Attacks

We have witnessed, in recent years, a disturbing trend in Indian cinema with the films that promote hypernationalism, glorify selective versions of history, and reduce patriotism to anti-Pakistan rhetoric. In theatres, audiences erupt into slogans of “Anti-Pakistan” and “Jai Shri Ram,” turning cinema halls into arenas for political and religious expression. Whether the subject is the Army, the Air Force, or a distorted retelling of historical and political events that conveniently glorifies contemporary politicians, the underlying message often seems less about patriotism and more about propaganda.

The very definition of patriotism appears to have undergone a transformation, particularly in Bollywood. Films that claim to portray India's history and political realities increasingly seem to offer selective narratives shaped by majoritarian, right-wing ideologies. In the process, Bollywood appears to have forgotten the remarkable patriotic films it once produced. Films that inspired love for the country without manufacturing hatred for another.

It is against this backdrop that #Prahaar comes as a refreshing and much-needed departure, an attempt at an honest, restrained narration of the horrific 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks.

Despite dealing with an emotionally charged subject, the film does not surrender to the temptation of hypernationalism. Instead, it takes us beyond India's borders and allows us to see the human side of the Pakistani prosecutors. This is not the familiar cinematic formula in which the humanity of Pakistani characters is selectively portrayed to establish the supposed moral superiority of Indian Muslims over their Pakistani counterparts. Rather, the film allows its characters and their circumstances to speak for themselves, without turning religion into a convenient instrument of political messaging.

Even when the film confronts us with the most horrific scenes of terror, violence, and loss of innocent lives, it does not manipulate us into hating an entire religion or community. And when the Indian judicial system's eventual success is portrayed, the film does not invite us to leap out of our seats in a manufactured frenzy of nationalistic triumph. It asks us to sit, watch, reflect, and absorb the gravity of what has unfolded before us.

Perhaps the film's greatest achievement is that it refuses to drug its audience with the familiar sedatives of manufactured patriotism. I found it difficult to believe, right until the end, that a film dealing with such a sensitive subject could resist the temptation to exploit hypernationalistic sentiments for commercial success, political mileage, or manufactured controversy. There are, of course, a couple of scenes featuring religious remarks, but they do not appear to be intended to incite hatred or provoke communal animosity. Instead, the film largely maintains a measured and responsible narrative.

That restraint deserves appreciation. At a time when cinema is increasingly being used to reinforce political narratives and deepen social divisions, a film that trusts its audience to think rather than dictates whom to hate is both courageous and necessary.

Rajkummar Rao is undoubtedly one of Bollywood's most remarkable actors, particularly when it comes to portraying real-life personalities and taking on uncompromising, hard-hitting stories. His performance in Shahid remains a testament to his ability to inhabit complex characters with conviction and sensitivity. In Prahaar, his portrayal of prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam is another commendable effort. He brings the character to life with a sense of seriousness and restraint that suits the gravity of the subject.

text:
JOHN NEWTON'S LETTERS

QUESTION:
What are the most obvious Causes, Symptoms, and Effects of a Decline in the Spiritual Life?

Believers are, by nature, dead in trespasses and sins, even as others—but, by faith in the Son of God, they are made partakers of a new and endless life. They derive it from him; and he has said, "Because I live, you shall live also." But the life of this life, if I may so speak, its manifestation and exercise, is subject to great changes. A sick man is still alive—but he has lost the cheerfulness, activity, and vigor which he possessed while he was in health. There are many people, who if they are, as we would hope, really alive to God—are at least sick, languid, and in a declining state. May the great Physician restore them! It is sometimes said, that "the knowledge of a disease amounts to half a remedy"; which will hold thus far in the present case, that unless we are sensible of our disorder and our danger—we shall not be heartily solicitous for a recovery.

The causes and symptoms or effects of such a decline are very numerous, nor is it always easy to distinguish them, for they have reciprocal influence to strengthen each other. What may be assigned as the cause, in many cases, is likewise a proof that the plague is already begun; and the effects may be considered as so many causes, which render the malady more confirmed, and more dangerous.
Among the many general CAUSES, we may assign a principal place to doctrinal error. I do not include every mistake or erroneous sentiment, which may be adopted or retained; but there are some errors, which, for the suddenness and violence of their operation, may be compared to 'poison'! Thus the Galatians, by listening to false teachers, were seduced from the simplicity of the gospel; the consequence was, that they quickly lost the blessedness they had once spoken of. Poison is seldom taken in the gross; but, if mingled with food, the mischief is not suspected until it is discovered by the effect.

Thus those who are employed in poisoning souls, generally make use of some important and beneficial truth, as a vehicle by which they convey their malignant drug into the minds of the unwary! Perhaps they speak well of the person and atonement of Christ, or they exalt the riches and freedom of divine grace—while under the veil of these fair pretenses, they insinuate prejudices against the nature or necessity of that holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord. Others speak strongly in general terms in favor of personal holiness—but their aim is to withdraw the heart from a dependence upon the Savior's blood, and the influences of his Holy Spirit, without which the most studied exactness of conduct, differs no less from the holiness of the gospel—than a picture or a statue, or a dead carcass, differs from a living man.

Whoever is thus prevailed upon, in the great and essential points of Scriptural doctrine—to separate, in his judgment and experience, those things which God has joined together, is already infected with a disease in its own nature mortal, and his religion, unless the Lord mercifully interposes, will degenerate into either licentiousness or formality!

We live in a day when too many are tossed to and fro, like ships without helm or pilot, by various winds of doctrine; and therefore those who wish well to their own souls, cannot be too much upon their guard against that spirit of curiosity and desire for 'new things', which the apostle describes by the metaphor of having itching ears, a desire of hearing every novel and singular teacher, lest they imbibe errors before they are aware, and become a prey to the sleight and craftiness of those who lie in wait to deceive!

Spiritual pride and self-admiration will likewise infallibly cause a declension in the divine life, though the mind may be preserved from the infection of doctrinal errors, and though the power of gospel truth may for a time have been really experienced. If our attainments in knowledge and giftedness, and even in grace—seduce us into a good opinion of ourselves, as if we were wise and good—we are already ensnared, in danger of falling every step we take, of mistaking the right path, and proceeding from bad to worse, without a power of correcting or even of discovering our deviations—unless and until the Lord mercifully interposes, by restoring us to a spirit of humility and dependence upon Himself. For God, who gives more grace to the humble—resists the proud! He beholds them with abhorrence—in proportion to the degree in which they admire themselves. It is the invariable law of his kingdom, that everyone who exalts himself—shall be abased.

True Christians, through the remaining evil of their hearts, and the subtle temptations of their enemy, are liable, not only to the workings of that pride which is common to our fallen nature—but to a certain kind of pride, which, though the most absurd and intolerable in any person, can only be found among those who make profession of the gospel. We have nothing but what we have received, and therefore to be proud of titles, wealth, knowledge, success, or any temporal advantages, by which the providence of God has distinguished us—is downright sinful! And for those who confess themselves to be 'sinners', and therefore deserving of nothing but misery and wrath—to be proud of those peculiar blessings which are derived from the gospel of his grace, is a wickedness of which even the demons are not capable of!

The apostle Paul was so aware of his danger of being exalted above measure, through the abundant revelations and peculiar favors which the Lord had afforded him, that he says, "There was given me a messenger of Satan to buffet me." He speaks of this sharp dispensation as an additional mercy, because he saw it was necessary, and designed to keep him humble and attentive to his own weakness.

Ministers who are honored with singular abilities and success, have great need of watchfulness and prayer on this account. The Lord sees not as man sees. Simple-hearted hearers are apt to admire their favorite preacher, and almost to consider him as something more than man in the pulpit, taking it for granted that he is deeply affected himself with the truths, which, with so much apparent liberty and power, he proposes to them; while, perhaps, the poor worm is secretly indulging self-applause, and pleasing himself with the numbers and attention of those who hang upon his words!

Perhaps such thoughts will occasionally rise in the minds of the best ministers; but, if they are allowed, if they become habitual, and enter strongly into the idea he forms of his own character; and if, while he professes to preach Christ Jesus the Lord—he is preaching himself, and seeking his own glory—he is guilty of high treason against the Majesty of him in whose name he speaks. And sooner or later, the effects of his pride will be visible and noticed. Errors in judgment, gross misconduct, and abatement of zeal, of gifts, of influence, are evils, always to be dreaded, when spiritual pride has gained an ascendancy, whether in public or in private life. "For who makes you different from anyone else? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you did not?" 1 Corinthians 4:7 "The Lord Almighty has planned it, to bring low the pride of all glory and to humble all who are renowned on the earth." Isaiah 23:9

An inordinate desire and attachment to the things of this present world, may be assigned as a third prevailing cause of a spiritual declension. Unless this evil principle is mortified in its root—by the doctrine of the cross—it will in time prevail over the most splendid profession. That love of the world, which is inconsistent with the true love of God—manifests itself in two different ways, as men by temper and habit are differently inclined:

The first is covetousness or greediness for gain. This was the ruin of Judas, and probably the cause of the defection of Demas. By the honorable mention made of him in some of Paul's epistles, Demas seems to have had much of Paul's confidence and esteem for a season. Yet at length his covetous passion prevailed, and the last account we have of him from the apostle, is, "Demas has deserted me—because he loved this present world." 2 Timothy 4:10

Again, there are people not chargeable with the love of money for its own sake—for they rather squander it—than hoard it. Yet they are equally under the influence of a worldly spirit! They manifest their worldly hearts—by an expensive taste in the articles of dress, furniture and feasting—which are always unsuitable to a Christian profession.

It is not easy to exactly mark out the precise line of Christian conduct in these respects, which befits the different situations in which the providence of God has placed us. Nor is it necessary, to those who are poor in spirit—and upright in heart. A simple desire of pleasing God, and adorning the gospel, will solve most cases of how a believer should spend his money—which occupy little and trifling minds. The inclination of our heart—will always direct and regulate our voluntary expenses. Those who love the Lord, and whose spirits are lively in His service, will avoid both stinginess and selfish extravagance. They will rather lean to the frugal side in how they spend their money on themselves—that they may be better able to promote God's cause, and to relieve the necessities of His people.

Misers, who can be content with the mere form of religion, will hoard all they can save—in order to gratify their avarice! Others will spend all they can spare—to gratify their vanity, or their worldly appetites!

It is not easy to determine which of these evils is the greatest. Perhaps of the two, the miser is least accessible to conviction, and consequently the most difficult to be reclaimed. But a desire for extravagance and indulgence, if persisted in, will gradually lead to such compliances with the spirit and maxims of the world, as will certainly weaken, if not wholly suppress—the exercise of vital godliness. In whatever degree the "love of the world" prevails—the "health of the soul" will proportionably decline.

"People who long to be rich, fall into temptation and are trapped by many foolish and harmful desires that plunge them into ruin and destruction. For the love of money is at the root of all kinds of evil. And some people, craving money, have wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows!" 1 Timothy 6:9-10.

Many other causes might be enumerated—but most of them may be reduced to the heads I have already mentioned. The practice of a single sin, or the omission of a single duty—if allowed against the light of conscience, and, if habitual, will be sufficient to keep the soul weak, unfruitful, and uncomfortable, and lay it open to the impression of every surrounding temptation. Sometimes unfaithfulness to light already received, perverts the judgment, and then errors which seem to afford some countenance or plea for a sin which the heart will not give up, are readily embraced, to evade the remonstrances of conscience. At other times, errors, incautiously admitted, imperceptibly weaken the sense of duty, and by degrees, spread their influences over the whole conduct. Faith and a good conscience are frequently mentioned together by the apostle, for they are inseparable; to part with one is to part with both. Those who hold the mystery of faith in a pure conscience, shall be preserved in a thriving frame of spirit, they shall grow in grace, go on from strength to strength, shall walk honorably and comfortably. But so far as the doctrines or the rules of the gospel are neglected, a wasting sickness will prey upon the vitals of religion, a sickness, in its nature mortal, and from which none recover—but those on whom God mercifully bestows the grace of repentance unto life.

The SYMPTOMS of such a soul sickness are very numerous and diversified, as tempers and situations vary. A few of those which are more generally apparent, and sure indications of a decline in religion are the following.
Bodily sickness is usually attended with loss of appetite, inactivity, and restlessness. Likewise, the sickness of the soul deprives it of rest and peace, causes a dullness and indolence in the service of God, and an indisposition to the means of grace, to secret waiting upon God, and to the public ordinances. These appointments, so necessary to preserve spiritual health, are either gradually neglected and given up, or the attendance upon them dwindles into a mere formal round, without relish and without benefit.

To the healthy man, plain food is savory—but the palate, when vitiated by sickness, becomes picky and fastidious, and hankers after varieties and delicacies. Likewise, when the sincere milk of the gospel, plain truth delivered in plain words, is no longer pleasing—but a person requires curious speculations, or the frothy eloquence of man's wisdom, to engage his attention, it is a bad sign. For these are suited to nourish, not the constitution—but the disease.

From slighting or trifling with those means which God has provided to satisfy the soul—the next step usually is—to seek relief from a compliance with the spirit, customs, and amusements of the world. And these compliances, when once allowed, will soon be defended; and those who cannot approve or imitate such conformity, will be represented as under the influence of a narrow, legal, or pharisaic spirit.

The sick professor is in a delirium, which prevents him from feeling his disease—and he rather supposes the alteration in his conduct is owing to an increase of wisdom, light, and liberty. He considers the time when he was more strict and circumspect as a time of ignorance, will smile at the recollection of what he now deems his childish scruples, and congratulates himself that he has happily outgrown them, and now finds that the services of God and the world are not so incompatible as he once thought them to be.

Yet while he thus relaxes the rule of his own conduct, he is a critically severe observer of the behavior of others. He sharply censures the miscarriages and even the mistakes of ministers and professors, if an occasion offers, and speaks of these things, not weeping as the apostle did—but with pleasure, and labors to persuade himself, that the strictness so much talked of, is either a cloak of hypocrisy, or the fruit of superstition. True Christians seldom meet with more uncandid misconstruction, or undeserved reproach, than from those who, having once been their companions, afterwards desert them.

When the disorder is at this height, it is truly dangerous, and indeed, as to any human help, desperate. But power belongs to God. May it please him to remember in mercy those who are near unto death, to restore them to their right minds, and to recover them to himself. Otherwise, "it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them!"

text:
Rapid Refactoring with Claude: https://t.co/79u2UD2IfE

😱 Claude and I wrote our own long-running task runner for Tollbooth MCPs. This week, we ripped it out and replaced it in minutes.

❓Tollbooth DPYC MCPs needed an asynchronous Task Runner for long-running tool requests which need more time than the conventions of synchronous HTTP TCP requests will tolerate. For example, in eXcalibur, a service for generating X posts, a post can hold a dynamic block whose text is an LLM prompt. Resolving that block often takes minutes: the LLM model needs to survey the web, analyze responses, synthesize and compose marketing content, and returns professional "copy".

However, as is common in industry, the Tollbooth DPYC MCPs are deployed as on-demand, serverless instances. This infrastructure has demanding synchronous response deadlines and it recycles containers. Work started in the context of one request does not reliably outlive the request. (In fact, it reliably dies at the end of the request response.)

🛠️ So Claude and I built a deferred execution task runner service with tools for the client to specify jobs, check job status, and to claim finished jobs. The runtime sealed a job description with AES-256-GCM, shipped the ciphertext to a generic remote flow, and that flow interpreted a small vocabulary of operations. Results came back through the platform's artifact store, because its own result storage was the worker's local disk and unreadable from anywhere else. A per-operator secret block held the seal key. A non-secret selector rode in the clear so the shared flow could pick the right one.

It took seven rather complex concepts to move one function call out of the synchronous flow into an asynchronous runner.

Every one of these concepts existed for a defensible reason. The remote flow could not execute our code. So we invented a wire format and an interpreter to describe our code to it.

It worked - but...

💥 It also failed in ways that were hard to observe and diagnose. A dispatch error fell back to running in the calling MCP process, which looked healthy but was a fakeout. So, we responded by adding instrumentation. Then more instrumentation. Then instrumentation for the instrumentation. We got better at observing a tortured implementation rather than implementing a better solution. That's a code smell whose stink gets more and more intolerable.

🔎 Two announcements made us look up. Anthropic shipped Managed Agents. Deno released celld, self-hosted Durable Objects.

These are attractive - but, after consideration, neither fit.

❌ Managed Agents runs Claude only, and we route every model call through our choice of LLM provider using (rockstar) OpenRouter. Any technology that is wedded to Anthropic is a non-starter.

❌ celld and Cloudflare Workflows offer TypeScript language support - but not Python. Adopting them would mean having to have second implementations for our encryption services, as well as for any code that we would want to be able to run "in process" or via async runners. Two implementations of one algorithm is killer-drift just waiting to happen.

😁 Fortunately, these technologies did something better than just fitting: they inspired us to write each other the requirements for our capability, which we had never actually shared with each other (Claude and me). Those are:

- Accept a request synchronously.
- Allow running for tens to hundreds of minutes.
- Let the client come back later and claim the answer.
- Nothing in that path may be bound to a synchronous HTTP deadline.
- Support Python, because our operators are Python.
- Be Model agnostic.
- Require no new stateful infrastructure.
- Offer Per-operator isolation.

Stated clearly, the field of candidate solutions thinned quickly. (Which we kind of knew because that is why we started this by writing our own solution without doing really good research.)

Temporal, Hatchet, Restate, DBOS, Kitaru. All capable durable-execution engines. Supported by the Pydantic Team, too - very comforting.

But, every one of them still needs a worker or a cluster that we would have to self host or at least provision.

Kitaru came closest in spirit, with checkpoints and a wait() that releases compute to zero while even waiting for a human to participate in the flow. Really nice.

Kitaru's current available hosting targets are Kubernetes and the big clouds. We will keep watching it. Setting up a cluster is too much of a heavy-lift for Tollbooth DPYC Operators.

⚡ Modal won. It's the one that ran our code.

In Modal, a decorator annotation marks a function as runnable asynchronously. The method spawn() returns a handle in milliseconds. Functions can run up to twenty-four hours. Billing is per second and scales to zero. The handle can be redeemed from any process, which is precisely the claim check our tools already hand out.

(According to Claude) the refactoring in the MCPs was a mere three lines. Where the old code started a background task, the new code spawns. The determination about which requests need long-running that we had already written did not change at all. What changed is only where execution occurs.

👍 Deleting the obsolete code for our own runner removed 1,940 lines from the tollbooth-dpyc Python wheel. The runtime module alone lost 511. Gone: the sealed closure, the key selector, the per-operator secret block, the operation vocabulary, the interpreter flow, the artifact result channel, the result shaper.

The DRY elegance matters more than the line count. We had been maintaining two implementations of one resolution. One ran in process. The other was baked into a sealed specification for the remote interpreter, with a third function to translate its answers back. Same behaviour, three places to keep in step. Now there is one registration and one path.

🔑 The identity story is the part we like best.

The Modal container requires only one secret: the operator's Nostr nsec. From that it derives its npub, finds its Authority's configuration DM on a Nostr relay, and receives its database URL and its vault key. We copy no database URL. We copy no encryption key. The container ends up holding exactly what the MCP host holds, and the operator's human only ever handles the one value they already know (the nsec of their Operator).

We also looked at MCP Tasks, the emerging standard for starting a long call and polling it. In the 2026-07-28 release candidate it moved out of the core specification and became an extension after a redesign, and anyone who shipped against the earlier version has to migrate. We kept our own claim-check tools for now and will adopt the standard once it settles.

Economically, for pricing tools to Patron users, the toll fares did not change. The tools did not change. The Operator remains at liberty to set prices dynamically based on the infrastructure expenses for using Modal.

😎 eXcalibur's dynamic Posts stopped dying and our Observability headaches stopped flaring up.

────────────────────

⚡  With Tollbooth DPYC, your patrons purchase, out of band, tranches of "𝐴𝑃𝐼 𝑆𝑎𝑡𝑠", using rapid-settlement Lightning. Patrons then spend these API Sats across different tool calls with zero per-request friction and no KYC.

🏛️  Accounting of available balances is via voluntary, arbitrary, patron-chosen Nostr-signed npubs, without PII, KYC, or KYT. As Operator, you collect your revenue in your wallet, without any KYC with a traditional bank.

Dive retailers, training agencies, resort marketers, and liveaboard operators can see the Wrap firsthand at Booth 617 in the First-Floor Exhibit Hall.

Weezle It’s a Wrap is an oversized insulated outer layer built for the time divers spend out of the water. Made in the U.K., its long, hooded shape can be worn over clothing for warmth between dives or used as a changing garment on the boat deck, dock, or beach. The Wrap is designed for surface use and complements, rather than replaces, a drysuit undersuit.

The Wrap draws on the same proven materials found in Snugpak’s Weezle Undersuit line, which debuted at last year’s DEMA Show. A Paratex® Light nylon outer is lightweight, highly windproof, water-repellent, and breathable, with a durable water-repellent finish. Inside, Softie® Premier synthetic insulation traps air to help retain warmth even when wet, while a luxurious suede-like Thermal Suede 1 (TS1) polyester lining grabs moisture from the skin for rapid drying without chilling.

External side pockets: keep small items close at hand.

Internal adjustment: gathers loose fabric and reduces flapping in the wind when worn as an outer layer.

Compression sack included: keeps the Wrap compact for travel and dive-bag storage.

For dive centers, charter operators, and travel retailers, the Wrap offers a surface-side companion to the Weezle Undersuit range, giving customers a single, packable answer for staying warm from the last ascent to the next giant stride.

It tells kids to find a “safe adult” outside the family, summarizes emancipation options, and says they do not have to convince their parents because these groups are ready to become their “found family.” Those organizations actually exist. They run youth programs. They affirm gender identity. Hatch works with children as young as elementary age. OutYouth and Resource Center offer spaces for teens. TENT has a FOR REAL Trans Texas Takeover tour of advocacy teach-ins, the same tour listed in the mailer.

Parental authority is not optional. The body is not a problem for activists to fix. Coaching minors to work around their parents on this issue is demonic.

I don’t care who mailed it! I care that the light of Christ shines on the agenda it promotes.

text:
Discover Egypt, a land where thousands of years of history unfold at every turn, from the age of the pharaohs and the construction of the pyramids to the influences of the Greeks, Romans, Ottomans, and modern Egyptians. Marvel at iconic landmarks such as the Giza Plateau, home to the Great Pyramid and the legendary Sphinx, explore Luxor's awe-inspiring Karnak Temple Complex and the Valley of the Kings, and uncover Alexandria's fascinating Greco-Roman heritage. Egypt's story stretches unbroken across millennia, blending Ancient Egyptian civilization with Coptic Christianity, magnificent Islamic architecture, and enduring traditions expressed through music, handicrafts, cuisine, and storytelling.

People & Culture: Egypt is renowned for its warm hospitality, deeply rooted family values, and lively social atmosphere. Visitors will experience the contrast between the bustling modern energy of Cairo and Alexandria and the slower-paced rhythms of life along the Nile and in rural villages. Hospitality is an important part of Egyptian culture, and guests are often welcomed with tea or coffee. Cultural customs include dressing modestly when visiting religious sites, exchanging handshakes and sometimes cheek kisses among friends, bargaining in traditional markets, and showing respect for local traditions and community life.

Cuisine: Egyptian cuisine is both comforting and flavorful, offering a rich blend of ancient traditions and regional influences. Signature dishes include koshari, a beloved street-food favorite made with rice, lentils, pasta, chickpeas, and spiced tomato sauce; ful medames, slow-cooked fava beans commonly enjoyed for breakfast; ta'ameya, Egypt's distinctive falafel made from fava beans rather than chickpeas; and molokhiya, a savory green stew served alongside rice or bread. Meat lovers will enjoy grilled kofta and kebabs, while dessert enthusiasts should sample local favorites such as basbousa and umm ali. Refreshing beverages include traditional mint tea, vibrant karkade (hibiscus tea), and freshly pressed sugarcane juice. For the ultimate culinary experience, consider joining a street-food tour in Cairo, sharing a home-cooked meal with a local family, or enjoying authentic Egyptian specialties while cruising along the Nile.

Best Time to Visit & Booking Advice: The most comfortable time to visit Egypt is between October and April, when milder temperatures make sightseeing, archaeological exploration, and desert adventures far more enjoyable. The summer months from May through September bring intense heat, particularly in Upper Egypt around Luxor and Aswan. However, travelers willing to embrace the warmer weather may benefit from lower prices and fewer crowds. For travel during the peak season, it is recommended to book international airfare and sought-after accommodations 3 to 6 months in advance. For holiday travel during December, Easter, and Eid celebrations, booking 6 to 9 months ahead is strongly advised. Nile cruises and private guided tours should also be reserved early to secure preferred vessels, itineraries, and expert guides.

Top 5 Must-Do Experiences in Egypt

1. Visit the Giza Pyramids & Great Sphinx
 Stand before one of the world's most recognizable landmarks and, if possible, venture inside one of the ancient pyramids. A camel or horseback ride across the plateau at sunset offers unforgettable views and spectacular photo opportunities.

2. Explore Luxor & the Valley of the Kings
 Discover the resting places of Egypt's greatest rulers, including the treasures associated with Tutankhamun. Wander the restored Avenue of Sphinxes and experience the grandeur of Karnak Temple at sunrise or sunset.

3. Sail the Nile Between Luxor and Aswan
 A Nile cruise combines cultural exploration with relaxation, allowing travelers to visit remarkable sites such as Edfu and Kom Ombo while enjoying beautiful river scenery.

4. Visit Abu Simbel
 Admire the colossal rock-cut temples of Ramses II and Queen Nefertari, among Egypt's most impressive archaeological wonders. Early morning visits provide the best experience and lighting.

5. Experience Cairo's Historic Bazaars & Islamic Quarter
 Browse the vibrant stalls of Khan El Khalili, admire centuries-old mosques including Al-Azhar, and enjoy traditional cafés where locals gather for conversation, tea, and shisha.

Accommodation Costs (Approximate)

For Couples:

Upscale accommodations, including quality four-star hotels and boutique properties, typically range from $150–$300 per night.
Luxury hotels, premium Nile cruise suites, and internationally recognized five-star properties generally range from $350–$800+ per night.
For a seven-night stay, expect to budget approximately $1,050–$2,100 for upscale accommodations and $2,450–$5,600+ for luxury experiences.

For Families of Four:

Upscale family accommodations or connecting rooms typically range from $250–$500 per night.
Luxury suites or multiple-room accommodations generally range from $450–$1,600+ per night.
A seven-night stay will typically cost between $1,750–$3,500 for upscale options and $3,150–$11,200+ for luxury properties.

Airfare from the Continental United States (Approximate)

Round-trip economy fares to Egypt generally range from $700–$1,200 per person, depending on travel dates, departure city, and airline. Business class fares commonly start around $2,500 and can exceed $6,000.

While nonstop service between the United States and Egypt remains limited, direct flights may be available from select major gateways such as New York. Most itineraries connect through major European or Middle Eastern hubs, including London, Paris, Istanbul, Doha, or Dubai. Total travel times generally range from 10 to 16+ hours, depending on routing and layover length.

Couples: Approximately $1,400–$2,400 total economy airfare.
Families of Four: Approximately $2,800–$4,800 total economy airfare.

Travel Tips & Practical Information
Purchase comprehensive travel insurance that includes medical coverage and trip interruption protection.
Verify visa requirements prior to departure. Many travelers can obtain an e-visa or visa upon arrival, though requirements vary by nationality.
Consult current CDC recommendations regarding vaccinations and health precautions.
Pack lightweight, breathable clothing, sun protection, comfortable walking shoes, and a reusable water bottle.
Always ask permission before photographing local people, particularly women and families.
Dress respectfully when visiting mosques, churches, and other religious sites.
